item.title: Southern California Edison warns of potential wildfire-related power shutoffs
item.description: An Edison International-owned electric utility could shut off power for up to 245,700 customers in parts of Southern California to reduce wildfire risk, the largest number under consideration for a potential public safety outage this year.
item.dc:creator: Varun Sahay
item.content:encoded: An Edison International-owned (EIX.N) electric utility could shut off power for up to 245,700 customers in parts of Southern California to reduce wildfire risk, the largest number under consideration for a potential public safety outage this year. Southern California Edison said on Wednesday strong winds and dry conditions in portions of Los Angeles, Santa Barbara, Ventura, Kern and Tulare counties could increase wildfire risk between Wednesday and Friday. Here are more details: Southern California Edison has not yet decided whether to implement shutoffs and said the decision would be based on real-time weather and wildfire conditions The utility said it monitors wind speeds, vegetation dryness and relative humidity when evaluating potential shutoffs Southern California Edison uses about 2,000 weather stations, 200 wildfire cameras and ground patrols to monitor high fire-risk areas If shutoffs are implemented, crews will inspect power lines and equipment before restoring service — a process that typically takes up to eight hours, but could be longer if damage is found or additional inspections are required The utility said wildfire mitigation efforts include undergrounding power lines and installing covered conductors to reduce wildfire risk and the need for future shutoffs "We have a responsibility to keep our community safe from the devastating impacts of wildfires," Southern California Edison spokesperson David Eisenhauer told Reuters "PSPS (public safety power shutoff) significantly reduces the risk that equipment could start an ignition during extreme weather," Eisenhauer said

item.title: What is Starshield, SpaceX's military version of Starlink?
item.description: Ukraine said on Wednesday that Elon Musk's SpaceX had restricted military-grade Starlink services, hampering Ukrainian drone strike missions and air defenses.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ukraine said on Wednesday that Elon Musk's [USN:L8N4600M6 TEXT:"SpaceX had restricted "military-grade" Starlink services"], hampering Ukrainian drone strike missions and air defenses. The complaint has drawn renewed attention to the distinction between Starlink, SpaceX's commercial satellite internet service, and Starshield, a military version developed for the Pentagon. While Musk has said the two systems are separate, in many cases they share the same underlying satellite technology. "Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government," Musk said on Wednesday in a post on X, adding that any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military or the president. "Starlink is a commercial service owned and controlled by SpaceX. Usage of Starlink is limited to civilian or defensive activities and cannot be used for offensive military action, as doing so would be inappropriate for a commercial company." WHAT IS STARLINK? Starlink, the main profit engine of SpaceX (SPCX.O) , is a satellite internet network of more than 11,000 satellites that beam broadband service directly to user terminals about the size of a folded newspaper. Its roughly 13 million subscribers range from households and hikers to shipping companies and major airlines. Since launching its first Starlink satellites in 2019 aboard reusable SpaceX rockets, the company has built a vast low-Earth-orbit constellation that blankets much of the planet, delivering faster connections than traditional communications satellites, which typically operate much farther from Earth and in far smaller numbers. Starlink gave Ukraine a critical communications advantage early in the war, reshaping how militaries operate on the battlefield. But Musk has restricted Starlink for certain military uses while highlighting Starshield, a more secure network developed for government and military missions. WHAT IS STARSHIELD? Starshield is a SpaceX business unit that develops military and intelligence satellite systems for the Pentagon. While its missions are separate from Starlink's commercial broadband service, the distinction is not always clear-cut: Starshield's secure communications services use enhanced encryption and dedicated terminals, but rely on the vast Starlink constellation as their backbone. Starshield leverages the technology, engineering and operational experiences of Starlink, according to SpaceX. In addition to secure communications, the company says the militarized version can also provide users with Earth observation and the ability to integrate sensors or other payloads. The Pentagon, Starshield's largest customer, has spent billions of dollars on both Starlink and Starshield services. It has also bought dedicated Starshield satellites, including communications spacecraft for missile-warning missions and a spy constellation for the National Reconnaissance Office, Reuters reported in 2024. Questions over the relationship between Starlink and Starshield have persisted since [USN:L1N31S38K TEXT:"Russia threatened Western satellites supporting Ukraine in 2022"]. SpaceX unveiled Starshield later that year, but the secrecy surrounding national security space programs has left the precise boundaries between the two systems opaque. Those distinctions became a point of contention earlier this year when the [USN:L6N41W1B2 TEXT:"Pentagon clashed with SpaceX over higher prices for satellite services"] used by military drones during the Iran conflict, Reuters reported. SpaceX argued that some customers paying roughly $5,000 per terminal for Starlink should instead have been using a Starshield service costing about $25,000 per terminal. [USN:L6N4290XG TEXT:"Britain has also adopted Starshield"]. Under that arrangement, the service uses the same satellite constellation, ground stations and terrestrial infrastructure as Starlink, but operates through dedicated terminals and separate network gateways, Britain’s defence ministry has told Reuters. Other US partners are evaluating the system as well. New Zealand is doing a trial of Starshield to assess its usefulness for military operations, the New Zealand Defence Force previously told Reuters.

item.title: É montagem vídeo de Lula defendendo prender trabalhadores
item.description: Um vídeo de um discurso do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) foi adulterado para simular que ele defendeu prender trabalhadores e proteger criminosos. A montagem inverte a ordem das palavras do candidato à reeleição.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Um vídeo de um discurso do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) foi adulterado para simular que ele defendeu prender trabalhadores e proteger criminosos. A montagem inverte a ordem das palavras do candidato à reeleição. Estes são os principais detalhes: O vídeo editado, que circula no Facebook , indica que Lula afirmou que o novo lema de sua campanha é “para o trabalhador, a prisão; para o bandido, a proteção”. As imagens são de um discurso do presidente em uma plenária com parlamentares no último dia 7. A transmissão ao vivo do pronunciamento no canal de Lula no YouTube e registros na imprensa mostram que o presidente defendeu proteger trabalhadores e prender criminosos, e não o contrário. “E o nosso lema é o seguinte: para o povo trabalhador, a proteção; para o bandido, a prisão”, disse Lula ao mencionar propostas de campanha para a segurança pública. Veredicto: Alterado digitalmente. Lula defendeu prender criminosos e proteger trabalhadores, e não o contrário. Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. item.title: Guyanese opposition leader arrested after shots fired outside home of police official
item.description: Guyanese opposition leader Azruddin Mohamed and two other men have been arrested following an exchange of gunfire outside the home of a senior police officer who is testifying in a U.S. extradition case against Mohamed, the South American country's government and police said.
item.dc:creator: Kemol King
item.content:encoded: Guyanese opposition leader Azruddin Mohamed and two other men have been arrested following an exchange of gunfire outside the home of a senior police officer who is testifying in a U.S. extradition case against Mohamed, the South American country's government and police said. US prosecutors allege Mohamed and his father Nazar Mohamed conspired to commit fraud and launder money through their gold exporting firm, Mohamed’s Enterprise, to enrich themselves and defraud the government of Guyana. The two men, who were indicted in Florida, have denied wrongdoing and are contesting their [USN:L6N3YR0WY TEXT:"extradition proceedings"] in court. The younger Mohamed has accused the government of persecuting him because of his entry into politics. His office on Wednesday denied possession of the firearm involved in the incident, accused police of planting it and alleged the three men were assaulted and threatened. Mohamed and the other men were arrested overnight on Tuesday after Senior Superintendent of Police, Prem Narine, who is testifying in the extradition proceedings, observed a vehicle passing his residence. The vehicle later returned, according to a Tuesday statement from the Guyana Police Force, and Narine heard what he believed to be a gunshot as the vehicle approached. Narine took cover, the statement said, and fired several rounds towards the car, which drove away. Officers later intercepted the vehicle, arresting Mohamed and the other men traveling in it. A search uncovered a firearm and ammunition, the police said. The government said in a separate statement on Tuesday that Mohamed and his companions had been filming Narine’s residence. It alleged that shots came from their vehicle and said the gun the police found was unlicensed. Mohamed's office described the shooting as an assassination attempt against Narine. Members of his We Invest in Nationhood party held a press conference on Wednesday to protest what they said was Mohamed's treatment by police. The party said he remains in custody. Mohamed, who has had multiple run-ins with the police since his extradition case began, was elected opposition leader in January. We Invest in Nationhood became the [USN:L2N3UU00K TEXT:"top opposition force"] in parliament in the 2025 general election, winning 16 of 65 seats.

item.title: Former portfolio manager sues Fidelity after leaving for Michael Dell's family office
item.description: A former semiconductor fund manager at Fidelity Investment Management has sued its parent company FMR, claiming it refused to pay him a "multimillion-dollar" compensation package after he joined DFO Management, the family office of billionaire Dell Technologies founder Michael Dell.
item.dc:creator: Suzanne McGee
item.content:encoded: A former semiconductor fund manager at Fidelity Investment Management has sued its parent company FMR, claiming it refused to pay him a "multimillion-dollar" compensation package after he joined DFO Management, the family office of billionaire Dell Technologies (DELL.N) founder Michael Dell. The suit, filed by Adam Benjamin in the Suffolk Division of the Superior Court of Massachusetts, alleges that after Fidelity executives failed to persuade him to stay at the firm, the company "turned on a dime" and terminated him on July 10 of this year. Fidelity then imposed a non-compete clause, causing him to forfeit a compensation package totaling in the millions of dollars. "Rather than protecting any legitimate business interests, the provisions are being broadly misused by Fidelity as a retention tool or improper barrier/deterrent to" Benjamin's ability to pursue other professional opportunities, the lawsuit alleges. Fidelity declined to comment on the lawsuit, which was filed on Friday. Neither Benjamin nor his lawyers could be reached for comment. Non-compete agreements are common in the asset management industry. Benjamin managed the $48 billion Fidelity Select Semiconductors Portfolio, which is up 58% so far this year, compared to 13.3% for the S&P 500 (.SPX) index. Its average annual return of 37.4% over the last five years puts it in the top percentile of all comparable funds rated by Morningstar, which awarded the fund five stars and a gold medalist rating, its top score. Benjamin began working at DFO on October 1, the lawsuit said. He alleged that Fidelity's withholding of compensation rests on the false claim that he was joining a competitor. He said he has never worked for Fidelity's own family office business.

item.title: US judge won't block Trump order targeting DEI by federal contractors
item.description: A federal judge declined on Wednesday to block an effort by President Donald Trump to eliminate diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives by companies that do business with the US government.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Wiessner
item.content:encoded: A federal judge declined on Wednesday to block an effort by President Donald Trump to eliminate diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives by companies that do business with the US government. US District Judge Adam Abelson in Baltimore, Maryland, said that groups representing university faculty and minority business owners had failed to show [USN:L1N40S0IR TEXT:"a March executive order"] by the Republican president was too broad. Trump's order bars [USN:FWN40E0ZQ TEXT:""racially discriminatory DEI activities""] by federal contractors and requires them to certify their compliance in writing. Businesses that do not comply could lose contracts and be investigated for violating the federal False Claims Act. The groups in their lawsuit claim that Trump's order wrongly presumes that all DEI amounts to illegal racial discrimination and extends to speech protected by the US Constitution. But Abelson said its definition of unlawful conduct was narrower. "The Contractors Order only prohibits contractors from engaging in conduct that is already prohibited by federal law: intentional discrimination on the basis of race or ethnicity," wrote Abelson, an appointee of President Joe Biden , a Democrat. The judge denied the groups' motion to block Trump's order pending the outcome of the lawsuit, which was filed in April. Democracy Forward, a progressive legal group that represents the plaintiffs, and the US Department of Justice did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Trump's order is also being challenged by 19 Democratic-led states and Washington, DC, in [USN:L1N42I0ZX TEXT:"a lawsuit in the same court"]. That case seeks to block federal agencies from altering contracts to comply with Trump's order. Many of the largest US businesses, from defense and tech companies to food service providers and logistics firms, are federal contractors, and some companies primarily depend on the government for work. Civil rights advocates say DEI practices help address historic inequities for marginalized groups like women, LGBTQ people and ethnic minorities. But Trump and many conservatives cast DEI [USN:L8N42O1L3 TEXT:"as anti-merit and discriminatory"] against groups like white people and men, and his administration has moved to eradicate it from government, higher education and the private sector. Trump has [USN:L1N3Z20XX TEXT:"banned DEI programs by federal agencies"] and repealed a 1965 executive order requiring federal contractors to take affirmative action to hire minorities and women.

item.title: Bond trading weakens for US banks as interest rate volatility affects investors
item.description: A steep selloff in the bond market showed up in Wall Street bank earnings during the last quarter, with some banks showing weaker fixed income trading as high interest rate volatility during the quarter curbed demand for transactions.
item.dc:creator: Tatiana Bautzer
item.content:encoded: A steep [USN:L8N45N0KW TEXT:"selloff in the bond market"] showed up in Wall Street bank earnings during the last quarter, with some banks showing weaker fixed income trading as high interest rate volatility during the quarter curbed demand for transactions. During the quarter, Treasury yields reached [USN:L6N45S11R TEXT:"multi-decade highs"] with some days showing abrupt moves in the market as investors repriced their expectations for where interest rates will go. At Morgan Stanley, revenues from fixed income, currencies and commodities trading (FICC) fell 7% in the quarter from a year earlier. [USN:L4N45Z0V1 TEXT:"At JPMorgan"], the drop was 4% and at [USN:L4N4600WF TEXT:"Bank of America"], 17%. [USN:L4N45Z0U6 TEXT:"Goldman Sachs"] had flat revenues with FICC trading. Citi was the odd one out, increasing its revenue 4% from a year earlier. "Interest rates rose pretty furiously throughout the third quarter, and it was unexpected versus where the market was in the second quarter", said Morgan Stanley Chief Financial Officer Sharon Yeshaya. There was less demand for structured transactions and the widening of credit spreads was a challenge to investors that have bond portfolios. Benchmark 10-year yields showed their [USN:L6N45M19U TEXT:"biggest quarterly rise since 2009"] at the end of September. "Reduced client activity and changing market conditions, including a major shift in interest rates, significantly affected our leading FICC businesses, including credit, mortgages and municipals," according to Bank of America Chief Financial Officer Alastair Borthwick. At Citigroup, most of the 4% growth in FICC trading revenue came from foreign exchange business and spread products. Citi CEO Jane Fraser told analysts rates revenue "was pressured by the trading environment, but we saw good growth in forex and spread products, both stable revenue streams." Another effect of [USN:L1N45U12M TEXT:"rising long-term yields"] on the banks' balance sheets was the higher volume of unrealized losses in securities portfolios. [USN:L4N4600XY TEXT:"Bank of America, for example"], showed unrealized losses on its bond portfolio - mortgage-backed securities and US Treasury, government-agency bonds - at $109 billion in the quarter ended September, up from $85 billion at the end of June, as bond yields rose in the last quarter. The bulk of these securities were in held-to-maturity segment, which the bank does not intend to sell. EQUITIES SHINE The results contrasted with that from equities trading desks, which brought eye-popping revenue growth in the quarter. At Goldman Sachs, equity trading revenue rose 72%, with higher revenues in derivatives and financing. Morgan Stanley equity revenues grew 41% and JPMorgan's, 49%. Bank of America and Citi had the lowest equity trading revenues growth, 11% and 14%, respectively. Oppenheimer analyst Chris Kotowski sees increased risk in the reliance on equity revenues, that may be volatile. "We do fear that there is an 'easy come, easy go' risk with these revenues," he wrote in a note to clients.

item.title: Dinamarca diz que exploração de recursos pelos EUA na Groenlândia precisa respeitar leis locais
item.description: O Ministério das Relações Exteriores da Dinamarca afirmou nesta quarta-feira que, caso os EUA desejassem explorar os recursos da Groenlândia, teriam que fazê-lo dentro do marco da legislação da ilha ártica, acrescentando que o acordo assinado no mês passado entre as três partes não alterou essa situação.
item.dc:creator: Louise Rasmussen
item.content:encoded: O Ministério das Relações Exteriores da Dinamarca afirmou nesta quarta-feira que, caso os EUA desejassem explorar os recursos da Groenlândia, teriam que fazê-lo dentro do marco da legislação da ilha ártica, acrescentando que o acordo assinado no mês passado entre as três partes não alterou essa situação. O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, afirmou nesta quarta-feira que uma “exploração em grande escala de petróleo, gás e minerais” estava prestes a começar na Groenlândia — uma declaração polêmica sobre um território que tem resistido aos seus esforços para controlá-lo e proibiu novas perfurações em busca de petróleo bruto. Trump descreveu a ilha ártica dinamarquesa, administrada por um governo semiautônomo, como “nossa nova e bela Groenlândia” em uma postagem nas redes sociais que elogiava o que ele chamou de ganhos dos EUA decorrentes de um acordo de segurança assinado em setembro. O Ministério das Relações Exteriores da Dinamarca afirmou em comunicado que “o acordo não concede aos investidores dos EUA qualquer tratamento preferencial em comparação com investidores de outros países da Otan, da União Europeia e de parceiros da Otan no que diz respeito ao acesso aos recursos naturais da Groenlândia”. O gabinete do primeiro-ministro da Groenlândia se recusou a comentar a declaração de Trump, enquanto o Ministério de Recursos Minerais da Groenlândia não respondeu imediatamente aos pedidos de comentário.

item.title: Biocon settles Roche's US patent lawsuit over proposed breast-cancer drug copy
item.description: Roche's Genentech has settled a US lawsuit against Indian biopharmaceutical company Biocon over its proposed biosimilar of Genentech's blockbuster breast-cancer drug Perjeta, Biocon said Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Blake Brittain
item.content:encoded: Roche's (ROPC.S) Genentech has settled a US lawsuit against Indian biopharmaceutical company Biocon (BION.NS) over its proposed biosimilar of Genentech's blockbuster breast-cancer drug Perjeta, Biocon said Wednesday. Biocon said in a statement that the settlement gives it the "earliest licensed launch dates" for a Perjeta biosimilar, allowing the company to launch its Pebrilzo in the first quarter of 2027 in the UK and European Union, and the third quarter of 2028 in the United States The release said that other terms of the agreement are confidential Biosimilars are versions of biologic drugs that are comparable to generics of traditional pharmaceuticals. Unlike traditional drugs, complex biologic drugs are made from living cells and cannot be copied exactly Genentech's biologic Perjeta was Switzerland-based Roche's sixth-best-selling drug last year, earning it nearly CHF 2.97 billion ($3.67 billion) in revenue worldwide, according to a company report Genentech [USN:L6N43W11Z TEXT:"sued Biocon"] in New Jersey earlier this year, alleging Biocon's biosimilar would infringe its patents The court dismissed the lawsuit on Wednesday at Genentech's request Biocon did not respond to Genentech's allegations in court The case is Genentech Inc v. Biocon Biologics Inc, US District Court for the District of New Jersey, No. 2:26-cv-09585 For Genentech: Michael Morin of Latham & Watkins For Biocon: Jeanna Wacker of Kirkland & Ellis Read more: [USN:L6N43W11Z TEXT:"Roche sues Biocon over proposed breast-cancer drug copy"]

item.title: As Ukraine struggles with Starlink and US satellite data, Europe has no quick fix
item.description: As Ukraine reported problems with Starlink satellite internet terminals and US data that warns of Russian ballistic missile attacks, Kyiv also faced the harsh reality that its European allies cannot offer any ready-made alternatives.
item.dc:creator: Vaishnavi Hajari, Gianluca Lo Nostro, Cassell Bryan-Low
item.content:encoded: As Ukraine [USN:L8N4600M6 TEXT:"reported problems"] with Starlink satellite internet terminals and US data that warns of Russian ballistic missile attacks, Kyiv also faced the harsh reality that its European allies cannot offer any ready-made alternatives. Ukrainian officials said on Wednesday the functioning of Starlink’s military-grade service Starshield had been interrupted when terminals were moving at high speed, hampering Ukrainian drones for attack missions and air defence. Separately, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said that, for the second night running, Ukraine had received no warning from its partners of a Russian ballistic missile attack on Kyiv. The reasons for the difficulties were not immediately clear but followed another souring of relations between US President Donald Trump and Ukraine, after Trump announced a deal to waive sanctions on Russian diesel and called for Zelenskiy to be replaced. Trump said on Tuesday that the United States was still sharing intelligence with Ukraine. Elon Musk and his SpaceX company had no immediate comment on Ukraine’s assertions. European countries have voiced strong support for Ukraine and Zelenskiy. But the problems with vital data highlighted that Ukraine and Europe depend heavily on US systems for both low-orbit satellite communications — provided by SpaceX via Starlink — and space-based infrared sensing that feeds into early-warning systems. A US satellite constellation called the Space-Based Infrared System provides early missile warnings. “That is fairly unique and … what basically that can detect is the heat generated by missiles as they're launched,” said Marc DeVore, an associate fellow at think tank Chatham House. “There is nothing equivalent in Europe.” NO SIMPLE STARLINK SWAP FOR UKRAINE, EUROPE As for Starlink, Europe does not have a ready-made alternative that Ukrainian soldiers could attach to their drones, although European governments and companies are working on long-term options. Shares in European satellite operator Eutelsat [USN:L6N4600QK TEXT:"soared"] on Wednesday following news of Ukraine's difficulties with Starshield, fuelled by investor bets that European providers could benefit from growing strains between Washington and Kyiv. But Christian Freiherr von der Ropp, an independent satellite consultant, said Eutelsat's OneWeb network was [USN:L5N3PN1Q8 TEXT:"not well suited"] to wartime use. "Its current constellation remains rooted in an outdated architecture and technology conceived a decade ago, without any evolution of its underlying design," he said. "Capacity and performance constraints, combined with the cost, weight, bulk and power consumption of its user terminals, limit its suitability for frontline applications." Eutelsat did not respond to a request for comment. Von der Ropp also said switching networks would require replacing thousands of terminals, as Starlink and Starshield terminals use proprietary technology and could not simply connect to OneWeb. Bohdan Sas, co-founder of Ukrainian defence technology startup Buntar Aerospace, said the sudden interruption to Starshield services "highlights to almost every end user both in Ukraine and abroad you can’t rely solely on one solution that can be switched off.” “You need to have some kind of sovereign capabilities," he added, so that "you are not subject to somebody’s mood today.” Fears of over-reliance on US defence technology have grown in Europe in recent years, as Trump has threatened to quit the NATO military alliance just as European leaders see Russia posing the greatest threat to the continent in decades. European Defence Commissioner Andrius Kubilius said at a conference hosted by Politico in Brussels on Wednesday that the continent was "quite dependent on American space capabilities.” “The answer to that situation is to develop our own capabilities,” he added, mentioning the European Union's planned satellite constellation IRIS² and urging European countries to work together to avoid frustration. But that project is years from becoming operational even if everything goes according to plan, causing frustration among European government officials. Germany is developing its own military satellite constellation.

item.title: Barcola bags hat-trick as Liverpool thrash LASK 6-3
item.description: Liverpool's Bradley Barcola scored his first goals for the club with a hat-trick as they swept aside Champions League newcomers LASK 6-3 on Wednesday, spoiling the Austrian side's first home game in Europe's elite club competition.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Liverpool's Bradley Barcola scored his first goals for the club with a hat-trick as they swept aside Champions League newcomers LASK 6-3 on Wednesday, spoiling the Austrian side's first home game in Europe's elite club competition. Ronald Araujo also opened his Liverpool account, while Jeremie Frimpong headed home and Lewis Koumas scored after twice being denied by the offside flag as Andoni Iraola's side responded emphatically to Sunday's 3-0 Premier League defeat by Manchester City. That match was City's first since being found guilty of 114 breaches of financial rules and they host two-time defending champions Paris St Germain later on Wednesday. Barcola's hat-trick offered some welcome relief after a slow start to his Liverpool career, with the French forward facing growing scrutiny following his big-money move. Iraola will be less satisfied with Liverpool's defensive display after Florian Flecker struck twice in three second-half minutes and Robert Ljubicic also scored for LASK. Liverpool began their campaign with a 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid, while LASK suffered a narrow 1-0 defeat by AEK Athens in their opener in September.

item.title: Houthis bring the war to Riyadh
item.description: The Houthis say they are not finished. On Wednesday, the Iran-backed group promised to keep hitting Saudi airports and oil facilities and told civilians, workers and "international shipping companies" to leave them. The same day, loud booms were heard over Riyadh, and the Saudi-led coalition said it had shot down a ballistic missile aimed at the capital. The threat came a day after a strike on Saudi Aramco's headquarters in Dhahran. The energy ministry called it a limited fire, but sources told Reuters that the blaze spread across several floors. Aramco staff are now working from home.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Mills
item.content:encoded: The Houthis say they are not finished. On Wednesday, the Iran-backed group [USN:L6N4600LI TEXT:"promised to keep hitting"] Saudi airports and oil facilities and told civilians, workers and "international shipping companies" to leave them. The same day, loud booms were heard over Riyadh, and the Saudi-led coalition said it had shot down a ballistic missile aimed at the capital. The threat came a day after a strike on Saudi Aramco's headquarters in Dhahran. The energy ministry called it a limited fire, but sources told Reuters that the blaze spread across several floors. Aramco staff are now working from home. [USN:L8N460160 TEXT:"Pilgrims"] have been caught up in the attacks too. Footage of Saturday's blast at Riyadh airport showed many travelers in the white cloth ihram clothes worn on the journey to Mecca. Saudi media reported that a Bangladeshi imam leading a group of pilgrims was among the dead. The Houthis have promised to spare Mecca and Medina. Still, people at the Grand Mosque say the constant phone alerts make them anxious. Can Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's plan to remake the economy survive a war on his doorstep? Our analysis looks at how the kingdom got here, and the tough questions it now faces. Plus: why Saudi Arabia's missile alerts went quiet before the deadliest strike. And in our news briefing: Iran's new campaign against shipping, Yemen's overwhelmed hospitals and "Davos in the desert" going hybrid. NEWS BRIEFING Iran has shifted tactics to [USN:L8N45Z15J TEXT:"step up attacks on shipping"] in and beyond the Strait of Hormuz, aiming to keep oil prices high and sway the US midterms, two senior Iranian officials told Reuters. Attacks have surged to their highest since the war began, deepening risks to global energy supplies. Hospitals across Yemen are [USN:L6N4600LK TEXT:"overwhelmed by soaring war casualties"], and intensified fighting has cut off aid to around 800,000 people, relief agencies said. The renewed Houthi-government war, reignited by the US-Iran confrontation, has left the encircled city of Taiz short of food and medicine, prompting warnings of a humanitarian catastrophe. Saudi Arabia plans to make its flagship Future Investment Initiative conference this month a [USN:L6N45Z0WN TEXT:"hybrid event"], letting executives attend remotely after deadly attacks on Riyadh airport, sources said. The shift highlights how the escalating war with the Houthis is challenging the kingdom's push to attract investment and become a global events hub. ANALYSIS: AFTER A WEEK OF HOUTHI STRIKES, SAUDI ARABIA FACES TOUGH QUESTIONS Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis have brought the war to the heart of Saudi Arabia in the past week, repeatedly striking Riyadh's international airport and, on Tuesday night, hitting the headquarters of Saudi Aramco, the world's largest oil and gas company and the backbone of the Saudi economy. Saturday's strike on the airport killed at least 13 people and wounded more than 300, the deadliest attack in the kingdom in more than a decade. The barrage is testing Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's bet that he can overhaul the kingdom's economy while staying out of the region's wars. But the crisis did not come out of nowhere. It grew, in part, from an unfinished war in Yemen, a US security umbrella that keeps failing to open and an economic plan that the crown prince was already redrawing. The crown prince's Vision 2030 made big bets on costly, futuristic giga-projects meant to wean the kingdom's economy off oil. But by 2025, many of those projects were indefinitely on hold as the kingdom reworked its economic strategy. When the United States and Israel launched their war on Iran in February, Riyadh initially appeared likely to escape the worst of it. Tehran's missiles and drones struck some Saudi targets, but the heaviest damage was in the UAE, Qatar, Bahrain and Kuwait. With the Strait of Hormuz effectively shut, Aramco ran its East-West pipeline at its maximum capacity of 7 million barrels per day (bpd) and shipped exports out through the Red Sea. The company reported a 25% jump in first-quarter profit, the envy of producers in neighbouring Gulf states. Aramco's oil kept flowing largely because the Houthis, Riyadh's foe on its southern border, did not formally join the war. The kingdom's tankers loaded at Red Sea ports and sailed unimpeded through the Bab el-Mandeb chokepoint to Asia. But a truce between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition collapsed in early July. The group declared a naval blockade of Saudi Arabia, attacked Saudi vessels and the East-West pipeline and, most alarmingly, seized Yemen's Red Sea coastline and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. The crown prince then called President Donald Trump at least twice, seeking US military support to push back the group. He got intelligence and targeting support, not air strikes, in another reminder that the US security umbrella the kingdom had relied on for decades was no longer a sure bet. Nevertheless, the Saudi-backed Yemeni government launched an offensive against the Houthis earlier this month that has made slow gains, while the Houthis besieged Taiz. This week's strikes on the airport and Aramco's headquarters followed. The Houthis had declared such sites legitimate targets and, on Wednesday, called the attacks retaliation for Saudi strikes on Yemen. Events are still moving too quickly to tell how, or whether, Riyadh can stay the course. Can oil keep flowing to its Asian customers while the Houthis control the Bab el-Mandeb? Will investors come when foreign direct investment last year reached only a third of the crown prince's $100 billion target? Can a state that relies on Aramco's dividends pay for a war and an economic overhaul at the same time? And will Trump, who has hinted that Washington "may" join Saudi strikes, finally step in? CHART OF THE WEEK As Mohammed bin Salman tries to build the country's tourism profile and foreign countries issue travel advisories, Muslim pilgrims were still landing and flying out of Riyadh when [USN:S8N44G01P TEXT:"Houthis struck the capital's airport"]. The group has struck several other airports such as Dammam, Abha, Najran and Jazan. These attacks raised worries over civil aviation becoming a target in armed conflict. "This level of sustained intense attack on civil aviation is unprecedented," said Mark Zee, founder of OPSGROUP, a membership-based organization that provides aviation safety advice. "I think this requires us to rethink how we view the current risk picture, and tread very carefully," he said. Air traffic tracker Flightradar24 showed planes avoiding the city on Monday, though jets were crossing Saudi airspace and landing at top hub Jeddah on the country's west coast. Cancellations across all Saudi airports reached 46.4%, aviation analytics firm Cirium said. LAST WAVE: THE WARNINGS THAT NEVER CAME Saudi Arabia's [USN:L8N45X021 TEXT:"early warning system went silent"] even as Houthi attacks mounted. The kingdom's last public alert of an incoming attack went out on September 29, days before strikes on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport killed at least 13 people and wounded more than 300. The government has not explained why. But when officials from an allied Western government asked, Saudi authorities said the alerts were too disruptive and that many citizens had complained of being woken by them at night, two officials told Reuters. Even Western embassies, which send staff their own internal alerts, got no warning before Saturday's strike, the deadliest. The silence ended on Monday when civil defense issued new alerts for Riyadh and southern cities. Former US ambassador Michael Ratney said the lack of warnings "creates the very nervousness they are trying to avoid."

item.title: Eight US states sue OpenAI, claiming ChatGPT harms children
item.description: Iowa, Kansas and six other states said on Wednesday they had sued OpenAI in courts across the country over harms they say ChatGPT has caused to children, alleging the chatbot has coached children to harm themselves or others.
item.dc:creator: Diana Jones
item.content:encoded: Iowa, Kansas and six other states said on Wednesday they had sued OpenAI in courts across the country over harms they say ChatGPT has caused to children, alleging the chatbot has coached children to harm themselves or others. The lawsuits, which were filed in state courts, are seeking an order forcing OpenAI to make changes to how ChatGPT works for children. The states are also seeking an order forcing the company to give up profits it has generated from young users. Florida's attorney general was the first to sue OpenAI, bringing [USN:L6N429106 TEXT:"a lawsuit"] over similar claims in June. The company is also facing dozens of lawsuits alleging ChatGPT aided in mass shootings or other violence.

item.title: Libro Beige de la Fed muestra presiones inflacionarias en un contexto de alza del combustible
item.description: El mercado laboral estadounidense se mantuvo en un estado de baja contratación y pocos despidos, pero la inflación se intensificó en varias partes del país en las últimas semanas, según un informe de la Reserva Federal del miércoles, que subraya lo que se juega este mes el banco central, que debe decidir si sube las tasas de interés por segunda reunión consecutiva.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El mercado laboral estadounidense se mantuvo en un estado de baja contratación y pocos despidos, pero la inflación se intensificó en varias partes del país en las últimas semanas, según un informe de la Reserva Federal del miércoles, que subraya lo que se juega este mes el banco central, que debe decidir si sube las tasas de interés por segunda reunión consecutiva. Si bien empresas en gran parte del país tienen una perspectiva económica positiva, sus "expectativas tienden a ser de un crecimiento leve, con mayor peso en la manufactura y lastradas por incertidumbres persistentes", dijo la Reserva Federal en su último "Libro Beige", un compendio de datos basados en encuestas y comentarios de empresas recopilados por sus 12 bancos regionales, que ofrece a los responsables de la política monetaria una visión de las condiciones económicas actuales. "Las empresas informaron de altos precios del diésel y señalaron que los recargos por combustible estaban trasladando el aumento de los costos a de toda la cadena de suministro", dice el informe, que señala que tres de los 12 distritos de la Reserva Federal describieron el crecimiento de los precios como sólido y ocho como moderado, mientras que tres señalaron que se estaba "intensificando". "Los contactos en varios distritos también mencionaron la continua presión sobre los precios derivada de otras materias primas, los aranceles y los seguros", añade el informe. La encuesta también sirve como una especie de barómetro de las presiones económicas a las que se enfrentan los votantes estadounidenses antes de las elecciones legislativas del 3 de noviembre, que determinarán si el Partido Republicano del presidente Donald Trump mantiene el control del Congreso. El costo de la vida es el principal asunto que mencionan los votantes en una reciente encuesta de Reuters/Ipsos. El mes pasado, la Reserva Federal aumentó su tasa de interés oficial un cuarto de punto porcentual, situándola en el rango del 3,75% al 4, 00%, y la mayoría de los responsables de la política monetaria de los bancos centrales han indicado que probablemente será necesario otro aumento de las tasas este año, aunque probablemente no hasta diciembre. Sin embargo, los mercados financieros ahora dan prácticamente las mismas probabilidades de una subida de tasas en la reunión de la Reserva Federal del 27 y 28 de octubre, después de que datos publicados el miércoles mostraron que los precios al consumidor aumentaron un 3,7% en los 12 meses a septiembre, mucho más rápido que el objetivo del 2% del banco central y más que el pronóstico consensuado de los economistas encuestados por Reuters. El aumento del precio de la gasolina, derivado del conflicto de siete meses en Oriente Medio, fue en gran parte responsable del incremento del IPC, si bien el rápido aumento de los precios del software y los juguetes también apunta al impacto de la demanda impulsada por la inteligencia artificial y a los aranceles más elevados impuestos por la política comercial de la administración Trump. El creciente costo de los préstamos para comprar una vivienda representa una carga adicional para muchos hogares estadounidenses. La tasa promedio de una hipoteca a tasa fija a 30 años subió la semana pasada al 7,5%, el nivel más alto en casi tres años, según informó el miércoles la Asociación de Banqueros Hipotecarios. Los datos para el último Libro Beige de la Reserva Federal se recopilaron el 5 de octubre o antes.

item.title: Pesquisa do Fed mostra pressões de preços ganhando força em meio a alta de custos dos combustíveis
item.description: O mercado de trabalho dos EUA permaneceu estagnado em um cenário de poucas contratações e demissões em massa, enquanto a inflação se intensificava em várias regiões do país nas últimas semanas, segundo relatório divulgado na quarta-feira pelo Federal Reserve, ressaltando o que está em jogo enquanto o banco central avalia se deve realizar um segundo aumento consecutivo da taxa de juros ainda neste mês.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O mercado de trabalho dos EUA permaneceu estagnado em um cenário de poucas contratações e demissões em massa, enquanto a inflação se intensificava em várias regiões do país nas últimas semanas, segundo relatório divulgado na quarta-feira pelo Federal Reserve, ressaltando o que está em jogo enquanto o banco central avalia se deve realizar um segundo aumento consecutivo da taxa de juros ainda neste mês. Embora as empresas em grande parte do país tenham uma perspectiva positiva, suas “expectativas tendem a ser de um crescimento moderado, com ênfase no setor manufatureiro e prejudicadas por incertezas persistentes”, afirmou o Fed em seu mais recente relatório “Livro Bege”, um compêndio de dados baseados em pesquisas e comentários de empresas compilados por seus 12 bancos regionais para fornecer uma visão das condições econômicas. “As empresas relataram preços elevados do diesel e observaram que as sobretaxas de combustível estavam repassando os custos aumentados por toda a cadeia de suprimentos”, afirmou o relatório. Ele observou que 3 dos 12 distritos do Fed descreveram o aumento dos preços como robusto e 8 como moderado, com 3 deles observando que ele estava “se intensificando”. “Contatos em vários distritos também observaram pressão contínua sobre os preços proveniente de outras commodities, tarifas e seguros”, afirmou o relatório. A pesquisa também funciona como uma espécie de barômetro das pressões econômicas que os eleitores estão enfrentando antes das eleições de meio de mandato de 3 de novembro, que determinarão se o Partido Republicano do presidente Donald Trump manterá o controle do Congresso. O custo de vida é a principal questão citada pelos eleitores em uma pesquisa recente da Reuters/Ipsos. O Fed aumentou sua taxa básica de juros em 0,25 ponto percentual, para a faixa de 3,75% a 4,00%, no mês passado, e a maioria dos formuladores de política monetária indicou que provavelmente será necessário outro aumento este ano, embora provavelmente não antes de dezembro. Os mercados financeiros estão precificando uma probabilidade de cerca de 37% de um aumento dos juros na reunião do Fed de 27 a 28 de outubro, depois que dados divulgados nesta quarta-feira mostraram que os preços ao consumidor (CPI, na sigla em inglês) subiram 3,7% nos 12 meses até setembro, muito mais do que a meta de 2% do banco central e acima da previsão consensual dos economistas consultados pela Reuters. O aumento nos custos da gasolina devido à guerra no Oriente Médio foi o principal responsável pelo aumento do CPI, com os preços em rápida elevação de softwares e brinquedos também apontando para o impacto da demanda impulsionada pela IA e das tarifas mais altas sob a política comercial de Trump. O aumento do custo dos empréstimos para a compra de imóveis é um fardo adicional para muitas famílias americanas. A taxa média das hipotecas de taxa fixa de 30 anos subiu na semana passada para 7,5%, o nível mais alto em quase três anos, informou a Associação dos Bancos Hipotecários na quarta-feira. Os dados para o último “Livro Bege” foram coletados até 5 de outubro. (Reportagem de Ann Saphir)

item.title: Red hot CPI report fuels AI rout
item.description: Major AI stocks slumped on Wednesday following the latest hot US inflation report, highlighting investor concern about the risks posed by rising borrowing costs in this capital-intensive sector.
item.dc:creator: Chuck Mikolajczak, Darshan R, Shashwat Chauhan
item.content:encoded: Major AI stocks slumped on Wednesday following the latest [USN:L6N4600XF TEXT:"hot US inflation report"], highlighting investor concern about the risks posed by rising borrowing costs in this capital-intensive sector. Among the [USN:L4N4601KQ TEXT:"leading decliners"] were data center operator CoreWeave (CRWV.O) , which fell 16%, AI infrastructure provider Nebius (NBIS.O) , off 11%, cloud computing giant Oracle (ORCL.N) , down 9%, and AI server seller Dell Technologies (DELL.N) , down 11%. Together the declines erased some $80 billion of market value. The declines reflect the impact of tightening financial conditions, as well as the outsize gains scored by some of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom. Barclays on Wednesday downgraded Dell and two other enterprise hardware stocks, noting that Dell shares have quadrupled this year — part of an AI-fueled investor binge that has resulted in 16 stocks in the S&P 500 technology sector (.SPLRCT) at least doubling this year, according to Reuters calculations. Concern over rising borrowing costs also weighed on Wednesday's other big decliners. Selling has been particularly intense in CoreWeave, which has issued $22 billion of bonds and $26 billion of loans, according to LSEG data. A CoreWeave bond that was issued in June yielding 9.625% recently yielded 15%. "We're getting a whole lot of information suggesting that the largest AI companies may not be generating the earnings or revenue people anticipated, and I think that makes everyone nervous about companies like CoreWeave," said Kim Forrest, chief investment officer at Bokeh Capital Partners. Coreweave Chief Executive Officer Mike Intrator said in an internal memo the market is acting “irrationally” and that he remains confident in the AI cloud company, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday. Wednesday's rout is the latest sign of a market struggling to come to grips with the implications of high inflation at a time when AI-fueled corporate borrowing has helped push up global interest rates. Investors generally remain sanguine on the sector in part because its largest players, from chip maker Nvidia (NVDA.O) to the so-called [USN:L4N45T0NO TEXT:"hyperscalers"] — primarily Alphabet (GOOGL.O) , Microsoft (MSFT.O) , Meta (META.O) and Amazon (AMZN.O) — are highly profitable and widely perceived as well managed, despite concerns about debt. But higher rates will make borrowing and building costlier, a fact that is likely to hit unprofitable and less-profitable firms first. On Wednesday, US interest rates rose following the hot inflation report, pushing the 30-year yield as high as 5.63% before rates pulled back sharply in the afternoon. "I do think long rates above 5% and creeping towards 6% is a problem for the marginal borrower, I'll call them," said Ross Mayfield, investment strategy analyst at Baird, in an interview with Reuters. "It gets a lot harder for the tiers below the kind of big four hyperscalers." The Nasdaq (.IXIC) was down 2% on Wednesday afternoon, with Alphabet and the other major hyperscalers mostly down between around 2%. SpaceX (SPCX.O) , another major AI player, was down 3%. "I guess it's grown to a group of five now. SpaceX has kind of joined the party here to join in with like Meta and Microsoft and Google and Amazon," said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management. "Those five are spending like 75% of the money that's being invested in data centers here in the country. And those five are obviously putting all their profits and then some into these data centers and the returns they're generating from those are really good." Despite the strong economics of these firms and their investments, Ellerbroek said it's not surprising that investors remain skeptical about the AI buildout, in part because of the busts that have preceded this one, particularly the dot-com meltdown that started in 2000. "This select group of companies is driving most of the growth in the economy and the stock market, and they're investing so, so aggressively and investors just aren't really willing to pay for it or fully buy in to the extent that we saw in the late 90s or whatever when investors kind of lost their minds," Ellerbroek said. "Investors have definitely not lost their minds. They're being very cautious and I think selective."

item.title: Zelenskiy recebe apoio total do Reino Unido depois que Trump se voltou contra ele
item.description: Volodymyr Zelenskiy recebeu uma forte demonstração de apoio em Londres nesta quarta-feira, ao se reunir com o primeiro-ministro britânico, Andy Burnham, e o rei Charles, depois que as relações do líder ucraniano com os Estados Unidos sofreram uma brusca deterioração.
item.dc:creator: William James
item.content:encoded: Volodymyr Zelenskiy recebeu uma forte demonstração de apoio em Londres nesta quarta-feira, ao se reunir com o primeiro-ministro britânico, Andy Burnham, e o rei Charles, depois que as relações do líder ucraniano com os Estados Unidos sofreram uma brusca deterioração. Zelenskiy foi recebido com todas as honras, chegando ao Reino Unido após mais uma noite de intensos ataques russos e poucas horas depois de a Ucrânia acusar a SpaceX, de Elon Musk, de incapacitar seus drones ao limitar os serviços da Starlink. A demonstração diplomática, que incluiu uma audiência de 25 minutos com Charles e uma guarda de honra em Downing Street, ecoou a visita de Zelenskiy a Londres em fevereiro de 2025, logo após ele ter entrado em conflito com o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, e seu vice, JD Vance. No início da reunião desta quarta-feira em Downing Street, Zelenskiy disse que queria discutir as dificuldades relacionadas à Starlink e ao compartilhamento de informações de inteligência, e que a Ucrânia ainda contava com sua parceria com os Estados Unidos. Trump afirmou no fim de semana que Zelenskiy deveria ser substituído como líder da Ucrânia, dias depois de ter fechado um acordo com Moscou para suspender as sanções às exportações russas de diesel. O Reino Unido afirmou que não apoia o acordo entre os EUA e a Rússia sobre o diesel e pediu que os aliados mantenham a pressão econômica sobre Moscou. Em entrevista ao jornalista Piers Morgan, Zelenskiy disse que foi doloroso ver Trump tomar o partido da Rússia em detrimento da Ucrânia. Burnham disse que os últimos dias foram “muito sombrios e difíceis” para a Ucrânia, mas que o Reino Unido continuava sendo um aliado firme. “Estamos ao seu lado, e isso não vai mudar”, afirmou. Anteriormente, ele anunciou a entrega planejada de 45 milhões de libras (US$59,60 milhões) em mísseis terra-ar usados para atingir drones russos movidos a jato, com 10 milhões de libras desse pacote sendo liberados em regime de urgência para atender a uma necessidade imediata na Ucrânia. Burnham solicitou que as autoridades elaborassem novas sanções e ajuda militar, e seus ministros das Relações Exteriores e da Fazenda têm pressionado os aliados a seguirem o exemplo do Reino Unido na proibição de serviços marítimos que apoiem as exportações russas de gás natural liquefeito.

item.title: Illinois QB Katin Houser (hand) out 4-6 weeks
item.description: Illinois quarterback Katin Houser underwent a medical procedure on his right (throwing) hand and is expected to be sidelined for four to six weeks, head coach Bret Bielema announced Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Illinois quarterback Katin Houser underwent a medical procedure on his right (throwing) hand and is expected to be sidelined for four to six weeks, head coach Bret Bielema announced Wednesday. Houser sustained the injury while attempting to make a tackle on an interception return in the third quarter of Saturday's 38-37 overtime victory at Michigan State. Michael Clayton II replaced Houser and tossed a 25-yard touchdown pass to Hudson Clement on the first play of overtime in East Lansing, Mich. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns for Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten), which returns to action on Oct. 24 against Oregon in Champaign, Ill. "I had a long conversation with him Sunday night kind of about what it means to be a starting quarterback in this league and in college football," Bielema said of Clayton on Wednesday. "... Excited about his opportunity." Houser, a transfer from East Carolina who began his college career with Michigan State, has completed 66.3% of his passes for 1,440 yards with 12 touchdowns and four interceptions in six games this season. He also has rushed for 120 yards and two TDs. --Field Level Media

item.title: Jessica Pegula, Coco Gauff qualify for WTA Finals
item.description: Americans Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula both have qualified for the season-ending WTA Finals for a fifth straight year, the WTA announced Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Americans Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula both have qualified for the season-ending WTA Finals for a fifth straight year, the WTA announced Wednesday. Only eight players qualify to compete in singles at the Nov. 8-15 hard-court tournament in Indian Wells, Calif., which features a $15.5 million prize pool. Gauff defeated China's Qinwen Zheng to win the tournament in 2024, while Pegula lost to Poland's Iga Swiatek in the 2023 final. Gauff, 22, is ranked No. 5 in the world and has won just one title this season at the Cincinnati Open, where she defeated Pegula in straight sets in the final on Aug. 23. Pegula, 32, is ranked No. 4 in the world and has two titles this season at the Dubai Tennis Championships in February and the Charleston Open in March. Also qualified for the WTA Finals are defending champion and World No. 1 Elena Rybakina of Kazakhstan, Aryna Sabalenka of Belarus, Mirra Andreeva of Russia and Linda Noskova of the Czech Republic, with two spots still open. --Field level Media

item.title: Racial employment gap widened among new US lawyers, study finds
item.description: Longstanding racial gaps in US entry-level lawyer employment increased for 2025 graduates, with white law graduates securing jobs at a higher rate than their Black, Hispanic and Asian classmates, new data show.
item.dc:creator: Karen Sloan
item.content:encoded: Longstanding racial gaps in US entry-level lawyer employment increased for 2025 graduates, with white law graduates securing jobs at a higher rate than their Black, Hispanic and Asian classmates, new data show. More than 94% of 2025’s white law graduates found jobs within 10 months, compared to less than 91% of law graduates of color, according to figures released Wednesday by the National Association for Law Placement. Black law graduates had the lowest employment rate at 87%, down from nearly 90% in 2024, the NALP data showed. The employment rate for 2025 Hispanic law graduates was slightly over 91%, down from more than 92% the previous year. The employment rate for Asian law graduates held steady at about 92%. The relatively small cohort of Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander law graduates posted the highest employment rate at more than 96%. “A law degree should open doors, but NALP's latest report shows that those doors are not equally open to everyone,” NALP Executive Director Nikia Gray said in a statement after releasing the data. The law graduates of 2025 hit the job market amid the Trump administration’s widespread campaign to eliminate diversity, equity and inclusion programs in higher education, government and the private sector. In March 2025, the US Equal Employment Opportunity Commission [USN:L1N3Q010H TEXT:"demanded detailed hiring data from 20 major firms"], including applicant names and whether race or gender influenced their employment decisions. The US Federal Trade Commission earlier this year [USN:FWN3YV125 TEXT:"warned"] 42 major law firms that their hiring practices may violate federal antitrust law. Diversity Lab, a group that promoted diversity goals at law firms, [USN:L6N42D0S9 TEXT:"shuttered"] in June after coming under FTC scrutiny. Many major law firms have publicly withdrawn or altered their public references to diversity, equity and inclusion since Trump returned to the White House, a Reuters special report found . Nearly 50 US law firms that previously provided NALP with demographic data about their lawyers [USN:L6N40C159 TEXT:"declined to do so"] this year, with NALP attributing the drop to Trump’s crackdown on law firm DEI efforts. Additionally, the US Department of Education is [USN:L6N44I0V8 TEXT:"poised to revoke"] the American Bar Association’s status as the federally recognized accreditor of US law schools, partly because it says the ABA took too long to eliminate DEI standards for schools. According to the new NALP data, white law graduates outpaced every racial group except for Middle Eastern or North African law graduates in securing jobs that require passing the bar — considered the gold standard for legal employment. First-generation college students had a lower employment rate than law graduates whose parents attended college or law school. Read more: [USN:L6N40C159 TEXT:"Facing DEI pressures, some law firms shield data in latest diversity survey"] [USN:L6N42D0S9 TEXT:"Law firm diversity group shutters amid Trump's DEI crackdown"]

item.title: Vinicius recibe suspensión de cuatro partidos y se perderá el Clásico contra el Barcelona
item.description: Vinicius Jr. se perderá el primer Clásico de la temporada del Real Madrid contra el Barcelona, después de que la Comisión Disciplinaria de la Federación Española de Fútbol le impuso el miércoles una sanción de cuatro partidos al delantero brasileño.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Vinicius Jr. se perderá el primer Clásico de la temporada del Real Madrid contra el Barcelona, después de que la Comisión Disciplinaria de la Federación Española de Fútbol le impuso el miércoles una sanción de cuatro partidos al delantero brasileño. Vinicius fue expulsado por tirar del pelo a Nathan Saliba tras salir desde el banquillo en la victoria por 1-0 del sábado ante el Villarreal. La comisión le impuso una sanción de dos partidos por la tarjeta roja y le sumó otros dos por sus protestas al árbitro, según el informe disciplinario de la octava jornada de LaLiga. La suspensión deja a Vinicius fuera de los partidos de liga contra el Sevilla, el Barcelona, el Racing de Santander y el Valencia, y a su entrenador, José Mourinho, sin uno de sus delanteros más usados para el desplazamiento al Camp Nou. Vinicius ha sido titular en todos los partidos del Real Madrid esta temporada, salvo uno. Tras el incidente, pidió disculpas a sus compañeros y a la afición del Real Madrid a través de las redes sociales. El Clásico se disputará el 25 de octubre, cuando el Real Madrid viaje para enfrentarse al líder de la liga, el Barcelona. Seis puntos separan a ambos equipos en la clasificación.

item.title: Red Bull boss Laurent Mekies signs multi-year extension
item.description: Max Verstappen has committed to Red Bull's Formula 1 team through 2030, and now the four-time world champion knows he will have continuity, with team principal Laurent Mekies signing a multi-year extension.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Max Verstappen has committed to Red Bull's Formula 1 team through 2030, and now the four-time world champion knows he will have continuity, with team principal Laurent Mekies signing a multi-year extension. The team announced Wednesday that Mekies now is signed through the 2031 season. The 49-year-old Frenchman was promoted in July 2025 following Christian Horner's departure. Mekies had spent six years at Ferrari before joining Red Bull's sister team Racing Bulls in 2023. After watching McLaren claim the 2025 constructors' championship and Red Bull get off to a slow start under the new regulations this season, the team has made steady progress. Verstappen has won consecutive races and sits fourth in the drivers' standings, just eight points behind Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and 17 points behind Mercedes' George Russell. Red Bull's second driver, Isack Hadjar, is eighth in the standings despite missing three races due to injury. Red Bull is also now only seven points behind McLaren for third place in the constructors' standings. "I am incredibly proud to continue this journey with Oracle Red Bull Racing," Mekies said in a statement. "What makes this team special is the way everyone comes together in pursuit of the same goal, and I feel privileged to work alongside such a talented and committed group every day. "As we look ahead, we will continue to embrace the principles that define us: being free in our thinking, fast in our actions and bold in our decisions." Mekies, who has overseen car upgrades throughout this season, thanked Red Bull shareholders Chalerm Yoovidhya and Mark Mateschitz for their continued support. "The strength of Red Bull has always come from its people and from creating an environment where talented individuals can achieve extraordinary things together," Yoovidhya and Mateschitz said in a joint statement. "Laurent has played a crucial role in guiding the team through an important period of transition while maintaining the competitive spirit and the Red Bull principles that define us. "This extension reflects our confidence in his leadership and our shared belief in the long-term vision of the team. We are ambitious about what lies ahead and we are committed to building on this momentum together." --Field Level Media

item.title: Report: FIFA to amend rule that led to Folarin Balogun red-card overturn
item.description: Call it the Folarin Balogun rule.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Call it the Folarin Balogun rule. FIFA is changing its rules to prevent a repeat of the outcry sparked by the reversal of Balogun's red-card ban at this summer's World Cup, ESPN reported Wednesday. The United States forward's red card, and its mandatory one-match suspension, was overturned by FIFA's disciplinary committee and he was allowed to play in a round of 16 match on July 6 against Belgium, which won 4-1. He had received a direct red card in the 64th minute of a July 1 match for a foul on Bosnia and Herzegovina's Tarik Muharemovic. The U.S. went on to win 2-0 with 10 men in the round of 32, and Balogun was suspended for the next game. The controversy deepened when U.S. President Donald Trump admitted he had personally asked FIFA president Gianni Infantino to review the penalty. Infantino has claimed that the disciplinary committee's decision was made without his involvement. When the 37-member FIFA council meets on Thursday, a motion to prohibit future such suspensions of one-match bans will be at the top of the agenda, per ESPN. Even if FIFA amends the rule, the Balogun controversy isn't likely to disappear. FIFA vice president Debbie Hewitt is among the sport's leaders who have asked Infantino to release all documents related to the case. Thursday's FIFA council meeting is the first since Infantino came under fire this summer for a now-tabled plan to sell a 20% stake in the World Cup's commercial business to private investors. --Field Level Media

item.title: Fed survey shows price pressures intensifying amid rise in fuel costs
item.description: The US labor market remained stuck in a low-hire, low-fire state and inflation was intensifying across parts of the country in recent weeks, a Federal Reserve report showed on Wednesday, underscoring what's at stake as the central bank weighs whether to deliver a second straight interest rate hike later this month.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The US labor market remained stuck in a low-hire, low-fire state and inflation was intensifying across parts of the country in recent weeks, a Federal Reserve report showed on Wednesday, underscoring what's at stake as the central bank weighs whether to deliver a second straight interest rate hike later this month. While businesses in much of the country have a positive outlook, their "expectations tend to be for slight growth, weighted toward manufacturing and burdened by persistent uncertainties," the Fed said in its latest "Beige Book" report, a compendium of survey-based data and commentary from businesses compiled by its 12 regional banks to provide a read on economic conditions. "Firms reported elevated diesel prices and noted that fuel surcharges were passing on increased costs throughout the supply chain," said the report. It noted that three of the Fed's 12 districts described price growth as robust and eight as moderate, with three noting it was "intensifying." "Contacts in multiple Districts also noted continued price pressure from other commodities, tariffs, and insurance," it said. The survey also acts as something of a barometer for the economic pressures voters are dealing with ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, which will determine whether President Donald Trump's Republican Party maintains control of Congress. The cost of living is the top issue cited by voters in a recent [USN:L6N45T0W3 TEXT:"Reuters/Ipsos poll."] The Fed increased its policy rate by a quarter of a percentage point to the [USN:L6N4570XW TEXT:"3.75%-4.00% range"] last month, and most policymakers have indicated another hike will likely be needed this year, though probably not until December. Financial markets are pricing [USN:L6N4600VL TEXT:"about a 37% chance"] of a rate hike at the Fed's October 27-28 meeting after data on Wednesday showed [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"consumer prices"] rose 3.7% in the 12 months through September, far faster than the central bank's 2% target and above the consensus forecast of economists polled by Reuters. Higher gasoline costs from the Middle East war were largely to blame for the higher CPI reading, with fast-rising software and toy prices also pointing to the impact of AI-driven demand and higher tariffs under Trump's trade policy. The rising cost of borrowing to buy a home is an added burden for many US households. The average rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage rose last week to 7.5%, the highest in nearly three years, the Mortgage Bankers Association said on Wednesday. The data for the latest Beige Book was collected on or before October 5.

item.title: Lamar Jackson idle, Ravens hopeful he's ready for Browns
item.description: Lamar Jackson was not made available to media for his typical Wednesday afternoon interview session, but signs point to the Ravens having their starting quarterback on the field Sunday against the Browns.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Lamar Jackson was not made available to media for his typical Wednesday afternoon interview session, but signs point to the Ravens having their starting quarterback on the field Sunday against the Browns. Jackson was not on the field at the start of Wednesday's practice, but he has regularly been idle for the first workout of the week in past seasons. Jackson missed Week 5 recovering from an ankle injury that knocked him out of Baltimore's Week 4 win over the Titans in the first half. Tyler Huntley guided Baltimore to a win at Atlanta in Jackson's absence and will continue to take some reps with the starters this week. If he's able to suit up, Jackson will be going head-to-head with former Ravens offensive coordinator Todd Monken. The current Browns head coach said Wednesday he is preparing "for the Ravens" more than he's planning to stop Jackson. Monken did note the Ravens are slightly harder to defend at the moment with Jackson taking more snaps under center. Without a preset launch point in the pocket, defenses have to account for every angle with Jackson and be ready for bulldozing running back Derrick Henry to come straight downhill. Jackson did not practice last week but head coach Jesse Minter said the Ravens anticipated a shorter-term recovery period. Last week, Minter left the door open for Jackson to play even without practicing. --Field Level Media

item.title: GRANOS Soja retrocede en Chicago ante avance de la cosecha, a pesar del repunte de la demanda china
item.description: Los futuros del maíz y la soja estadounidenses bajaban el miércoles ya que el ritmo acelerado de la cosecha en el Medio Oeste aumentó la oferta, y se prevé que las condiciones meteorológicas sean en general favorables tras las lluvias caídas a mediados de semana en algunas zonas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Los futuros del maíz y la soja estadounidenses bajaban el miércoles ya que el ritmo acelerado de la cosecha en el Medio Oeste aumentó la oferta, y se prevé que las condiciones meteorológicas sean en general favorables tras las lluvias caídas a mediados de semana en algunas zonas. La caída en la soja se vio limitada por la noticia de que China había adquirido varios cargamentos estadounidenses, en lo que supone la primera compra importante desde la reunión comercial de alto nivel celebrada el mes pasado. El trigo subía ligeramente debido a las preocupaciones sobre el suministro procedente de Rusia y Ucrania, ya que los ataques a buques de carga han interrumpido los envíos desde la región del Mar Negro. El maíz y la soja siguen apoyados por la intensa actividad de cosecha en todo el Medio Oeste. El Departamento de Agricultura de Estados Unidos indicó que, al domingo, se había cosechado el 33% del maíz y el 46% de la soja del país, ya que los agricultores aprovecharon el tiempo más seco tras las lluvias que retrasaron la cosecha en septiembre. Las lluvias de esta semana han paralizado los trabajos en el campo, pero se espera que vuelva el clima más seco a finales de semana, según los meteorólogos. "Hoy hemos bajado debido al avance de la siembra y al hecho de que parece que vamos a tener buen clima de aquí en adelante. Pero nos mantenemos en niveles más bajos, dentro del rango de cotización. Los usuarios finales están intensificando sus compras en el mercado", afirmó Jack Scoville, analista de The Price Group. Los compradores del Gobierno chino contrataron entre 8 y 10 cargamentos de soja estadounidense el martes, dijeron operadores a Reuters. El Departamento de Agricultura estadounidense confirmó la mayor parte de las compras el miércoles en su comunicado diario de ventas de exportación. Los operadores están atentos a nuevas compras, ya que China se esfuerza por cumplir su compromiso de compra anual de 25 millones de toneladas métricas, en medio de la preocupación por el exceso de capacidad de trituración en el país. La Administración General de Aduanas de China informó de una caída del 7,7% en las importaciones de soja en septiembre. Los contratos de soja de noviembre de la Bolsa de Chicago bajaban 9 centavos a 12,7475 dólares por bushel a las 1715 GMT, mientras que los de maíz de diciembre cedían 3,50 centavos a 4,7925 dólares por bushel. El trigo de diciembre de la CBOT subía 2,50 centavos a 6,7175 dólares por bushel, tras conocerse la noticia de que dos buques de carga habían sido alcanzados por drones frente a la costa de Bulgaria.

item.title: Olivia Miles leads 6-player WNBA All-Rookie Team
item.description: Rookie of the Year and MVP runner-up Olivia Miles of the Minnesota Lynx headline the six-player 2026 WNBA All-Rookie Team, announced Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Rookie of the Year and MVP runner-up Olivia Miles of the Minnesota Lynx headline the six-player 2026 WNBA All-Rookie Team, announced Wednesday. Miles was joined by No. 1 overall draft pick Azzi Fudd of the Dallas Wings, Seattle Storm guard Flau'Jae Johnson, Chicago Sky guard Sydney Taylor, Toronto Tempo guard Kiki Rice and New York Liberty guard Pauline Astier. Rice and Astier tied for fifth in the voting. Miles, the No. 2 overall pick, made the All-Star team and averaged 19.8 points, 6.0 assists and 4.7 rebounds in 40 games (all starts). Fudd averaged 13.1 points and shot 39.7% from 3-point range in 30 games (24 starts). Johnson averaged 14.9 points, 4.8 rebounds and 2.9 assists in 42 games (all starts). Taylor, undrafted out of Louisville, posted 13.6 points and 2.0 assists in 37 games (26 starts). Rice averaged 13.4 points, 3.7 rebounds and 3.5 assists in 28 games (20 starts) for the expansion Tempo. Astier, undrafted out of France, played all 44 games (39 starts) and tallied 9.3 points, 3.3 assists and 2.7 rebounds. --Field Level Media

item.title: BofA's mega-fine blunted by Team Trump history
item.description: A $1.2 bln penalty over compliance issues often rattles bank boards and shareholders. Just ask erstwhile CEOs of Citi, TD and Wells Fargo. Boss Brian Moynihan's money-laundering mess leaves him in comparatively tepid water, given the administration's vexing signals on wrongdoing.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Gandel
item.content:encoded: Aesop's "Boy Who Cried Wolf" will be a treasured tale for Bank of America (BAC.N) CEO Brian Moynihan. The mega-lender he runs just copped to violating the Bank Secrecy Act with a deficient anti-money-laundering program, transgressions that include a $1.2 billion fine. Compliance matters of this magnitude tend to unnerve boards and shareholders, but the Trump administration's past pronouncements on financial wrongdoing dilute the moral of this particular story. The US Treasury Department and Office of the Comptroller of the Currency unveiled enforcement action on Tuesday, accusing BofA of failing to report more than $5 billion of suspicious transactions in a timely manner. The agencies levied one of their biggest-ever penalties because, they said, Moynihan and his team put revenue ahead of addressing concerns raised by regulators before. BofA said it is [USN:O8N43T02A TEXT:""far along with and committed to completing""] the related issues and already absorbed many of the costs, including hundreds of millions of dollars during the third quarter. Moynihan has some damage control to do, but he may be in relatively tepid water compared to erstwhile counterparts. Citigroup's (C.N) Michael Corbat, Wells Fargo's John Stumpf (WFC.N) and TD Bank's Bharat Masrani (TD.TO) all left their respective CEO roles after running into similarly significant regulatory problems. President Donald Trump's vexing track record, however, probably gives Moynihan extra wiggle room. It's easy to question the motivations here. For one thing, Trump [USN:FWN3W42W4 TEXT:"pardoned"] Binance founder Changpeng Zhao, who had pleaded guilty to anti-money-laundering violations and stepped down from the cryptocurrency exchange as part of a $4.3 billion settlement. Administration officials also have been echoing industry complaints that suspicious-activity reporting rules have become overly burdensome. Dubious probes like the one into former Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell have more than a whiff of political bullying. Moreover, just days into his second term, the president publicly [USN:S0N3OG012 TEXT:"rebuked"] Moynihan at the World Economic Forum in Davos for allegedly discriminating against conservative customers. Moynihan is under some justified pressure. BofA's share price gains have broadly under-performed the industry in recent years, prompting investors to push him to boost returns on tangible common equity into the high teens, even as some rivals already exceed 20%. The bank recently tried to [USN:L1N45V0WY TEXT:"reassure"] staff about deal-maker defections, Reuters reported this week. Even excluding the latest regulatory penalty, its third-quarter earnings would have declined, making it an outlier among large lenders. Although compliance shortcomings add to the CEO's challenges, the true extent of the problem is hard to discern because of who's shouting about them. As a result, Moynihan has scope to keep the real wolves at bay. Follow Stephen Gandel on LinkedIn and X . Bank of America on October 13 agreed to pay a $1.2 billion fine to settle accusations in a civil case brought by the financial crimes unit of the Treasury Department and Office of the Comptroller of the Currency that it failed to address previously flagged lapses in its anti-money-laundering controls. The US regulators said the bank failed to report in a timely way more than $5 billion of suspicious transactions to Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network. As part of the settlement, BofA admits that it willfully violated the Bank Secrecy Act and failed to implement and maintain an anti-money-laundering program that met minimum regulatory requirements, Treasury said in a statement. BofA is required to work with a third party to identify and report suspicious transactions that were undetected and undergo an independent review of its suspicious activity monitoring and other programs, according to the consent order.
