item.title: Vinicius Jr. ficará de fora de clássico contra Barcelona após suspensão de quatro partidas
item.description: Vinicius Jr. não poderá disputar o primeiro El Clásico, duelo que coloca frente à frente Real Madrid e Barcelona, da temporada, depois que a comissão disciplinar da Federação Espanhola de Futebol aplicou ao atacante brasileiro uma suspensão de quatro partidas nesta quarta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Vinicius Jr. não poderá disputar o primeiro El Clásico, duelo que coloca frente à frente Real Madrid e Barcelona, da temporada, depois que a comissão disciplinar da Federação Espanhola de Futebol aplicou ao atacante brasileiro uma suspensão de quatro partidas nesta quarta-feira. Vinicius foi expulso por puxar o cabelo de Nathan Saliba na vitória de 1 x 0 sobre o Villarreal, no sábado. A comissão impôs uma suspensão de duas partidas pela infração que resultou no cartão vermelho e acrescentou mais duas partidas por seus protestos contra o árbitro, de acordo com o relatório disciplinar referente à oitava rodada da LaLiga. A suspensão tira Vinícius das partidas do campeonato contra Sevilla, Barcelona, Racing Santander e Valencia, deixando o técnico José Mourinho sem um de seus atacantes mais utilizados para a viagem ao Camp Nou. Vinicius foi titular em todas as partidas do Real nesta temporada, com exceção de uma. Ele pediu desculpas aos companheiros de equipe e aos torcedores do Real Madrid nas redes sociais após o incidente. O El Clásico acontece no dia 25 de outubro, quando o Real viaja para enfrentar o líder do campeonato, o Barcelona. As equipes estão separadas por seis pontos na tabela. (Reportagem de Ruairidh Barlow)

item.title: AI-powered stock funds bet bots can pick stocks faster and better than humans
item.description: A handful of fund managers are betting that exchange traded funds run by AI stock-picking models can crunch data quicker and make better investment decisions than humans, even as many people remain wary or even fearful of artificial intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Suzanne McGee
item.content:encoded: A handful of fund managers are betting that exchange traded funds run by AI stock-picking models can crunch data quicker and make better investment decisions than humans, even as many people remain wary or even fearful of artificial intelligence. So far, fewer than half-a-dozen ETFs, collectively managing only about $30 million of the ETF industry's nearly $17 trillion in assets, rely solely on AI-powered bots to control everything from research to stock selection. While that represents a tiny fraction of the industry, AI is making its way slowly and steadily into the investment processes of most asset managers, to some extent, even if that may not yet be visible to investors themselves. Earlier this year, 91% of asset managers surveyed by Mercer reported plans to increase their use of AI-based portfolio management tools this year and said they are trying to figure out what tasks can be safely handed off to AI. The performance of the handful of funds that rely solely on AI to generate returns shows they are beating the market, even if their track records stretch back only a few months. Their managers argue these returns will attract more investments into the idea over time. "Until now you've had two choices: be a passive investor and own an index, or be an active investor" with a human picking stocks, said Tal Schwartz, founder and CEO of Ai Funds. "I want to offer a third option: where it's AI that is doing it all for you." In August, Schwartz launched the High Conviction US Equity AI-Managed ETF (HIAI.Z) , built on a proprietary AI learning algorithm that analyzes decades of market data. So far, it has attracted less than $20 million in assets, according to data from ETF.com, but Schwartz said it is still early days. AI can crunch more data more rapidly than any human being, he said, and strips human emotions and cognitive biases out of the investment process. "I know this is a long-term process, that people will only become convinced over time," he added. "I think that what will convince them is performance." Schwartz's fund is up 2.7% since its August 21 launch, beating the 1.1% gain for the S&P 500 index in the same time frame. Two funds [USN:L8N3Z61LG TEXT:"launched by Israeli asset manager"] FinQ in February have handily beaten the 11.0% gain by the S&P over that time frame. FinQ's dollar-neutral US Large-Cap AI-managed ETF (AINT.P) has soared 25.35% and the version of the ETF not offering a currency hedge is 23.98% higher since inception. Two other funds, the Pacer S&P 500 3AI Top 100 ETF (PSAI.Z) and the Pacer S&P World 3AI Top 100 ETF (WDAI.Z) , are ahead 10.34% and 10.33%, respectively, since their launches in early May, compared to a gain of 5.8% for the S&P 500. Nonetheless, advisers and analysts said the funds' short track records and above-average fees may limit investor interest. "Advisers are comfortable with AI that informs a decision and uneasy with AI that makes it," said Jeff Judge, a financial adviser at Chesapeake Financial Planners in Forest Hill, Maryland, adding his clients are not clamoring for this. "Proof that this approach works will really come down to who can thoughtfully manage risk and ride out a down market," said Todd Sohn, ETF analyst at Strategas. AI-ENHANCED ETFS MORE COMMON Other firms have rolled out "AI-enhanced" ETFs, which use AI to undertake quantitative analysis, analyze stocks or monitor risk. This cautious approach is more common, insiders said. "We've been training models using AI for seven or eight years now, and using them to run live capital for about four years," said David Wright, head of quantitative investments at Pictet Asset Management in Geneva. His firm launched the Pictet AI Enhanced US Equity ETF (PQUS.P) in February. Since its debut, the fund has attracted $163 million in assets and posted gains of 14.8%, compared to 11.4% for the S&P 500. Wright compares using AI in the investment process to using a plane's autopilot functions. The autopilot may be able to take off, cruise and land with no humans involved, but, he added, "I wouldn't go on a plane that didn't have a pilot." Other asset managers are taking a similarly cautious approach to integrating AI. "I'm not losing any sleep over robots ending the world," said Dan Taylor, deputy chief investment officer of systematic within Man Group, referring to recent headlines. "But I still do worry about AI's ability to deal with the most extreme, unlikely events, where all the action happens, both good and bad."

item.title: Valor global dos direitos de mídia esportiva atinge recorde de US$65,8 bilhões em 2026
item.description: O valor global dos direitos de mídia esportiva atingiu um recorde de US$65,82 bilhões em 2026, um aumento de 15% em relação a 2025, de acordo com o Relatório Global de Mídia Esportiva 2026 da SportBusiness, publicado nesta quarta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Streisand Neto
item.content:encoded: O valor global dos direitos de mídia esportiva atingiu um recorde de US$65,82 bilhões em 2026, um aumento de 15% em relação a 2025, de acordo com o Relatório Global de Mídia Esportiva 2026 da SportBusiness, publicado nesta quarta-feira. Dois grandes eventos esportivos ocorreram em 2026: a Copa do Mundo de futebol na América do Norte e os Jogos Olímpicos de Inverno. O relatório prevê que o valor global dos direitos de transmissão esportiva cairá para US$62,2 bilhões em 2027. Em comparação com o valor de US$62,4 bilhões em 2024, ano dos Jogos Olímpicos de Paris, o crescimento em dois anos foi de 5%, segundo o relatório anual. Os EUA detêm grande parte do valor global dos direitos de mídia e agora representam 53,9% do total mundial, contra 46% em 2022. Os cinco maiores mercados da Europa, juntos, representam um terço do valor dos EUA. Os esportes norte-americanos, principalmente a Liga Nacional de Futebol (NFL) e a Associação Nacional de Basquete (NBA), respondem, juntos, por 30% do valor total global dos direitos de mídia. A Premier League inglesa responde por 7,8%, segundo o relatório.

item.title: Hope ton powers Windies to series-levelling win over India
item.description: Shai Hope struck another century as West Indies beat India by 24 runs in the fourth Twenty20 in Hyderabad on Wednesday to level the five-match series at 2-2.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Shai Hope struck another century as West Indies beat India by 24 runs in the fourth Twenty20 in Hyderabad on Wednesday to level the five-match series at 2-2. Chasing 248, India made a brisk start with Sanju Samson racing to a half-century off 20 deliveries before falling to Keemo Paul for 56. Shreyas Iyer chipped in with 16 off 11 balls and Abhishek Sharma contributed 29 before Gudakesh Motie removed the opener. India accelerated again at the death through Nitish Kumar Reddy and Tilak Varma, who added 70 runs from 32 balls to keep the chase alive. Varma fell for 43 and Reddy was dismissed by Keemo Paul who triggered a collapse by claiming three wickets in the 19th over. India's tail folded quickly and the hosts were bowled out for 223. West Indies, put in to bat, made a brisk start with Jewel Andrew providing early impetus alongside captain Hope before Axar Patel trapped the opener LBW for 21 off 16 balls. Shimron Hetmyer and Hope added a rapid 58 runs, but Prince Yadav broke the stand with a caught-and-bowled effort to dismiss Hetmyer for a blistering 33 off 12 balls. Rovman Powell followed soon after, departing for 24. Hope remained unfazed, however, sharing an unbroken 91-run stand from 43 balls with Sherfane Rutherford who finished unbeaten on 49 off 26 deliveries. The hosts accelerated at the death, taking 22 runs off the 17th over to surge past the 200-run mark. Hope smashed an unbeaten 102 off 50 balls with four fours and nine sixes, reaching the milestone with a six off the final delivery as West Indies finished on 247 for three.

item.title: UN peacekeeping chief says talks on future of Lebanon mission must begin soon
item.description: UN peacekeeping chief Jean-Pierre Lacroix on Wednesday urged the UN Security Council to begin negotiations on the future of peacekeepers deployed in Lebanon, as Beirut campaigns for an extension to the mandate set to expire at the end of this year.
item.dc:creator: Maya Gebeily
item.content:encoded: UN peacekeeping chief Jean-Pierre Lacroix on Wednesday urged the UN Security Council to begin negotiations on the future of peacekeepers deployed in Lebanon, as Beirut campaigns for an extension to the mandate set to expire at the end of this year. A UN peacekeeping force known as UNIFIL has been deployed in southern Lebanon since 1978 but the Security Council last year ordered the mission to begin withdrawing at the end of 2026. Since a new war erupted in March between Israel and Iran-backed Lebanese armed group Hezbollah, the Lebanese government has campaigned for an extension to [USN:L6N45B03E TEXT:"UNIFIL's mandate"], citing its role in monitoring hostilities and facilitating [USN:L6N45502W TEXT:"aid deliveries"] to villages in Israeli-occupied zones. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres earlier this year [USN:L8N42A20H TEXT:"presented proposals"] for a continued uniformed UN presence in Lebanon but no action has been taken yet, Lacroix told Reuters in Beirut. "These proposals are on the table of the Security Council. There has been no movement in the Security Council until now, but I believe that the negotiations will begin ... shortly, in earnest," he said. "I think it would be better to have a decision soon rather than later, right? Because that would clarify also the horizon for us, certainly from the more limited point of view of our own planning," he said. FORCES OPERATE HOTLINE TO EASE TENSIONS Diplomats say the US is not supportive of an extended mandate for UNIFIL, but Lacroix said it was important to focus on Lebanon’s request and that negotiations at the Security Council could yield a constructive outcome. Some 7,500 UNIFIL peacekeepers are still deployed at about 50 positions in southern Lebanon, which would be expected to be handed over to Lebanese army troops if no new UN force is agreed. But since most of those posts lie in territory now occupied by the Israeli military, it remains unclear how Lebanese soldiers could deploy to take over the positions. Lacroix said that clarity on whether a new UN force would deploy to southern Lebanon would help UNIFIL make sure it does not "leave those positions prematurely before we know what could come next". In addition to facilitating aid deliveries and monitoring hostilities, the force operates a hotline to ease any tensions between the Lebanese and Israeli militaries. Lacroix said the deconfliction role was particularly crucial given the presence of Israeli troops in a self-declared security zone deep in Lebanese territory. He said that Israeli and Lebanese troops in the same geographic area presented "the risk of escalation, the risk of incidents getting out of control" and that "there is a need for a third party to de-escalate".

item.title: Brasil recebe US$2,415 bilhões líquidos na semana após o 1º turno, diz BC
item.description: O Brasil registrou fluxo cambial total positivo de US$3,214 bilhões em outubro até o dia 9, sendo que apenas na semana passada entraram no país US$2,415 bilhões líquidos, na esteira do resultado do primeiro turno da eleição presidencial.

item.content:encoded: O Brasil registrou fluxo cambial total positivo de US$3,214 bilhões em outubro até o dia 9, sendo que apenas na semana passada entraram no país US$2,415 bilhões líquidos, na esteira do resultado do primeiro turno da eleição presidencial. ACUMULADO DE OUTUBRO No acumulado de outubro até o dia 9, a entrada de recursos pelo canal financeiro somou US$4,087 bilhões, ante uma saída de US$872 milhões pela via comercial, mostraram os dados do BC. Os números são preliminares e fazem parte das estatísticas referentes ao câmbio contratado. Considerando o acumulado do ano até 9 de outubro, o Brasil registra fluxo cambial total positivo de US$13,916 bilhões.

Vinicius was sent off for pulling Nathan Saliba's hair after coming off the bench in Saturday's 1-0 win over Villarreal. The suspension rules Vinicius out of league matches against Sevilla, Barcelona, Racing Santander and Valencia, leaving coach Jose Mourinho without one of his most-used forwards for the trip to Camp Nou. Vinicius has started all but one of Real's matches this season. He [USN:L6N45W07P TEXT:"apologised"] to his teammates and Real Madrid fans on social media after the incident. The Clasico takes place on October 25, with Real travelling to face league leaders Barcelona. The teams are separated by six points in the table.

item.title: How does the US count measles deaths?
item.description: US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has changed how the federal government recognizes deaths from measles in the midst of the worst US outbreak of the highly infectious virus in more than three decades, prompting backlash from disease experts and political opponents.
item.dc:creator: Nancy Lapid
item.content:encoded: US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has changed how the federal government recognizes deaths from measles in the midst of the worst US outbreak of the highly infectious virus in more than three decades, prompting backlash from disease experts and political opponents. Here is what you need to know about how US measles deaths are currently determined: WHAT HAS CHANGED? For over a century, US state and local health officials have been required to report cases of death in people with a measles diagnosis to the federal government. These reports are separate from death certificates issued by hospital staff or coroners that can list measles as a cause of death or as a contributing factor. Disease experts have generally considered the death of any person infected with measles to be related to the virus, which can directly impair organs or exacerbate underlying health problems. Kennedy has said the US will no longer automatically include state reports to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention of people who died with measles in the national published tally of measles deaths. Instead, the CDC's National Center for Health Statistics will first confirm that measles was identified as an underlying cause of death on a person's death certificate — a process that can take weeks, according to health experts. The CDC has [USN:L4N45A17G TEXT:"also said"] it was re-evaluating how measles deaths are defined, without explaining the need for such a review. WHY IS KENNEDY'S CHANGE CONTROVERSIAL? After eradicating measles transmission within the country in 2000, the United States is now battling its biggest resurgence of the virus since 1991, fueled by rising vaccine hesitancy. More than 6,300 infections and at least eight fatalities have been reported by state and local officials since Kennedy, a longtime anti-vaccine activist, took the nation's top health job in early 2025. Kennedy, who spent years sowing doubt about the measles vaccine — by far the best way to prevent infection and spread of the disease — has cast doubt on whether measles can be fatal and promoted the theory that the virus is less dangerous than the vaccines used against it, contrary to decades of scientific evidence showing the benefits of the shots. He [USN:L6N45811F TEXT:"sparred publicly"] with Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro, a Democrat, over the state's report of [USN:L4N45Y144 TEXT:"measles-related deaths"] before changing how such fatalities are counted. The CDC has so far accepted only two out of five measles-related deaths reported by US states so far this year. Leading medical organizations say Kennedy's comments and policies on immunization have increased Americans' distrust of vaccines, despite decades of evidence showing they are safe and effective at preventing disease. Disease experts say that the health secretary's questioning of measles death reports minimizes the risks of the virus, and that the change in how deaths are counted will delay information that could persuade more families to vaccinate their children. WHY ISN'T IT OBVIOUS WHEN SOMEONE DIED FROM MEASLES? Many infectious diseases kill indirectly. Measles, for example, can trigger complications such as croup, pneumonia and brain swelling that ultimately prove fatal. In some cases, deadly neurological complications don't appear until years after the infection. The virus can also induce immune system suppression that makes patients vulnerable to fatal secondary bacterial and viral infections. Death certificates generally record a chain of events. When a patient dies of respiratory failure due to pneumonia that was due to measles, the respiratory failure is the immediate cause of death, and measles is considered an underlying cause because it initiated the sequence of events leading to death. Local public health officials generally focus on the underlying cause because it reflects the disease responsible for setting the fatal process in motion. WHAT IF THE PERSON HAD OTHER SERIOUS HEALTH PROBLEMS? When a person with chronic lung disease, cancer, or another condition that makes them especially vulnerable to severe complications dies after a measles infection, the central question is usually whether the death would likely have occurred if the person had not contracted the virus. Investigators must determine whether measles caused the fatal deterioration, merely contributed to it, or was unrelated. Two experts reviewing the same medical records may sometimes emphasize different aspects of the case. That does not necessarily mean either side is acting improperly. Cause-of-death determinations often involve medical judgment. WHAT IS THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A MEASLES DEATH AND A MEASLES-ASSOCIATED DEATH? The term "measles-associated death" can reflect uncertainty about precisely how much the virus contributed. It allows health officials to acknowledge a connection when multiple factors were involved. ARE MEASLES DEATHS BEING OVERCOUNTED? There is no evidence that measles mortality is systematically overcounted. Historically, public health surveillance has focused on whether a disease caused or substantially contributed to death, rather than whether it was the sole factor involved. During the height of the COVID-19 pandemic, a similar debate took place over whether patients with preexisting chronic diseases were dying from COVID — that is, the SARS-CoV-2 virus caused the death — or with COVID, meaning they happened to have COVID but their cancer or other health condition is what killed them. Public health experts argue that excluding deaths simply because a patient had other medical problems would underestimate the disease's impact.

item.title: Lucrative tennis exhibition postponed amid Middle East conflict
item.description: The third edition of the Six Kings Slam, a high-stakes men's tennis exhibition in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, will not go off as scheduled next week amid tensions in the Middle East.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The third edition of the Six Kings Slam, a high-stakes men's tennis exhibition in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, will not go off as scheduled next week amid tensions in the Middle East. The six-player tournament was scheduled for Oct. 21, 22 and 24 and has been moved to Dec. 27-30, according to a statement shared Wednesday on X by Turki Al-Sheikh, chairman of Saudi Arabia's General Entertainment Authority. The statement said the decision to reschedule the event came after "an assessment of the organizational and logistical challenges associated with hosting the tournament and their potential impact on the quality of the audience experience." In Riyadh, the capital of Saudi Arabia, the King Khalid International Airport is closed after it was struck by drone and missile attacks attributed to Houthi rebels from Yemen during the past week. The New York Times reported that at least 14 people have been killed and hundreds more injured in the Iran-backed attacks. The tournament was set to include Carlos Alcaraz, Novak Djokovic, Alexander Zverev, Taylor Fritz, Alex de Minaur and Learner Tien, the latter a replacement for the injured Jannik Sinner. It is not known whether the players have committed to the replacement dates. Each participant is guaranteed an appearance fee of $1.5 million, with the winner earning an additional $4.5 million. Sinner walked away with $6 million in each of the event's first two years, defeating Alcaraz in the final both times. --Field Level Media

item.title: Atlantic Ocean currents can recover from severe climate weakening, study finds
item.description: An Atlantic Ocean current system weakened by global warming could recover over time if the climate cools, a study by the Danish Meteorological Institute showed on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Agnieszka Olenska, Louise Rasmussen
item.content:encoded: An Atlantic Ocean current system weakened by global warming could recover over time if the climate cools, a study by the Danish Meteorological Institute showed on Wednesday. The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation brings warm water from the tropics northward toward the Arctic, and the flow of warm water helps keep Europe's winters mild. Published in the journal Science Advances, the study found no sign there was an irreversible tipping point for AMOC, as suggested by some previous studies, although the effects of the changes could last for centuries. However, it also said that the Greenland ice sheet that contributes to weakening the AMOC as it pours cold freshwater into the ocean could not be restored once it had melted — even if the warming trend was reversed. A disrupted AMOC could still destabilise global rainfall patterns and accelerate [USN:L6N3WM0K1 TEXT:"coastal sea-level rise"]. NO TIPPING POINT LEADING TO COLLAPSE SEEN IN MODEL The study said the AMOC could slow to about 6 million cubic metres of water per second from around 17 million at around 7 degrees Celsius of global warming. "In our model, we do not see a tipping point leading to a collapse. The AMOC gradually weakens, but we find that it also immediately regains its strength if global warming is reversed," lead author Chuncheng Guo said. However, he warned that even though recovery starts as soon as temperatures fall, it could take several centuries to finish, all while the effects of a weakened current would persist. The 7 C rise used in the modelling used for scientific interest is far beyond the current projections for the warming trend. The UN's environmental body said in September global temperature rises are set to exceed the key threshold of 1.5 C "within a few years". Governments committed to keeping temperature rises within 1.5 C to limit the impacts of extreme weather under the 2015 Paris Agreement. The cooling rate required to reverse the AMOC also exceeds what is considered realistic with current technology, Guo added, pointing to a limitation of the single-model study. Further testing against other models was also needed, the study said. Willem Huiskamp at the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research, who was not involved in the study, said a more stable AMOC would be good news, but said he doubted the real-world current was as stable as some models suggested. The researchers estimated a long-term sea-level rise of around 20 cm from the melting of the Greenland ice sheet following a 1.5 C rise, and urged faster action to rein in emissions. "Instead of relying on the global cooling to happen, it's a much, much safer strategy to not have warming in the first place," Guo said.

item.title: Juez federal bloquea la reorganización prevista de una agencia agrícola estadounidense
item.description: Un juez federal impidió el miércoles que el Departamento de Agricultura de Estados Unidos siguiera adelante con la reorganización prevista de la agencia, lo que supone un revés para la amplia reforma del poder ejecutivo impulsada por el presidente Donald Trump.
item.dc:creator: Leah Douglas
item.content:encoded: Un juez federal impidió el miércoles que el Departamento de Agricultura de Estados Unidos siguiera adelante con la reorganización prevista de la agencia, lo que supone un revés para la amplia reforma del poder ejecutivo impulsada por el presidente Donald Trump. La sentencia del Tribunal de Distrito del Distrito Norte de California supone una victoria para los sindicatos que habían presentado una demanda para bloquear la iniciativa de reorganización, en parte porque los empleados afirmaban que debilitaría los servicios de la agencia. La orden detiene los esfuerzos de reorganización en varias agencias del USDA, entre ellas el Servicio de Investigación Agrícola, el Servicio Forestal, la Administración de Alimentación y Nutrición y otras. El juez Vince Chhabria señaló que la agencia estaba "reprogramando" los fondos del Congreso destinados a la reorganización, es decir, utilizando el dinero para un fin distinto al previsto. "El Congreso no contemplaba que el USDA utilizara los fondos que le habían sido asignados para cerrar oficinas o reubicar a empleados", escribió Chhabria. La iniciativa de reorganización de la agencia tenía como objetivo trasladar a unos 2.600 empleados de la región de Washington, así como consolidar las oficinas de la agencia en todo el país. El personal de la agencia había advertido que las salidas masivas de empleados a causa de la reorganización ponían en riesgo los programas de comercio, ayuda exterior, nutrición y otros. Un portavoz del USDA declaró: "El Departamento está analizando la decisión del juez y presentará su respuesta ante el tribunal". "El intento de la Administración de desmantelar esta agencia esencial es flagrantemente ilegal, y agradecemos que el tribunal haya impedido, por ahora, que se lleve a cabo un plan temerario", declaró Patrick Moran, presidente de la Federación Estadounidense de Empleados Estatales, del Condado y Municipales, en un comunicado.

item.title: Patriots open window for A.J. Brown; Christian Gonzalez ready to return
item.description: The New England Patriots have opened the 21-day practice window for wide receiver A.J. Brown, head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The New England Patriots have opened the 21-day practice window for wide receiver A.J. Brown, head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters on Wednesday. Brown has been sidelined since sustaining a high-ankle sprain during the second half of the Patriots' 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks in the teams' season opener on Sept. 9. He went on injured reserve two days later and missed the team's last four games. While Brown is working his way back to game action, Pro Bowl cornerback Christian Gonzalez told reporters that he's ready to return to the field after missing two games due to a shoulder injury. "I'm good now, ready for Sunday," Gonzalez told reporters Wednesday. Gonzalez, 24, signed a four-year, $135 million contract extension last month. He has started all 37 career games in which he has played -- including three this season -- since being selected by New England with the 17th overall pick of the 2023 NFL Draft out of Oregon. The Patriots host their AFC East rivals, the New York Jets, on Sunday. As for Brown, he sustained his injury after he was targeted by a third-down pass from Drake Maye, but Seahawks nickel cornerback Nehemiah Pritchett deflected the pass to force a punt. Pritchett's knee landed on the outside of Brown's ankle, which twisted inward as he went to the ground. Acquired from the Philadelphia Eagles via trade in early June, Brown had three receptions for a team-high 26 yards in the first half. Brown, 29, was named second-team All-Pro with the Eagles in 2022, 2023 and 2024. He has 527 receptions for 8,055 yards and 56 touchdowns in 106 career games (98 starts) with the Tennessee Titans (2019-21), Eagles (2022-25) and Patriots. --Field Level Media

item.title: Report: Broncos S Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) out multiple weeks
item.description: Denver Broncos safety Talanoa Hufanga will miss two to three weeks with an ankle injury, ESPN reported on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Denver Broncos safety Talanoa Hufanga will miss two to three weeks with an ankle injury, ESPN reported on Wednesday. The former All-Pro sustained the injury during Denver's 23-17 road win against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday. Hufanga has been listed as a non-participant in practice this week and will likely be ruled out for Thursday night's game against the visiting Seattle Seahawks (3-2). Hufanga, 26, has recorded 23 tackles, two interceptions (one returned for a touchdown), a sack and a forced fumble through five starts for the Broncos (3-2). A fifth-round draft pick by San Francisco in 2021, Hufanga has 348 tackles, nine interceptions (two pick-sixes), five sacks and four forced fumbles in 71 career games (59 starts) with the 49ers (2021-24) and Broncos. He made the Pro Bowl and was named first-team All-Pro in 2022. The Denver depth chart at safety includes starter Brandon Jones, Devon Key, JL Skinner and Tycen Anderson. --Field Level Media

item.title: Los derechos de retransmisión deportiva alcanzaron un récord de 65.800 millones de dólares en 2026
item.description: El valor global de los derechos de retransmisión deportiva alcanzó un récord de 65.820 millones de dólares en 2026, un aumento del 15% frente al año previo, según el "SportBusiness Global Media Report 2026", gracias a dos grandes eventos: el Mundial de fútbol y los Juegos Olímpicos de Invierno.
item.dc:creator: Streisand Neto
item.content:encoded: El valor global de los derechos de retransmisión deportiva alcanzó un récord de 65.820 millones de dólares en 2026, un aumento del 15% frente al año previo, según el "SportBusiness Global Media Report 2026", gracias a dos grandes eventos: el Mundial de fútbol y los Juegos Olímpicos de Invierno. El informe, que se publicó el miércoles, prevé que el valor mundial de los derechos de retransmisión deportiva sumará 62.200 millones de dólares en 2027. En comparación con los 62.400 millones de dólares de 2024, el año de los Juegos Olímpicos de verano de París, el crecimiento en dos años ha sido del 5%, según el reporte anual. Estados Unidos concentra gran parte del valor mundial de los derechos de retransmisión y ahora representa el 53,9% del total mundial, frente al 46% de 2022. Los cinco mayores mercados europeos suman, en conjunto, un tercio del valor de Estados Unidos. Los deportes estadounidenses, sobre todo la NFL y la NBA, representan entre ambos el 30% del valor total de los derechos de retransmisión del mundo, mientras que la Premier League inglesa supone el 7,8%, según el informe.

item.title: Ministério Público abre apuração sobre moderação de conteúdo das eleições por Meta e X
item.description: O Ministério Público Federal (MPF) abriu um procedimento administrativo com o objetivo de apurar as práticas de moderação de conteúdo adotadas pelas empresas Meta e X durante as eleições de 2026, informou o órgão, após reclamações de bloqueios, suspensão de contas, remoções de publicações e restrições de alcance.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O Ministério Público Federal (MPF) abriu um procedimento administrativo com o objetivo de apurar as práticas de moderação de conteúdo adotadas pelas empresas Meta e X durante as eleições de 2026, informou o órgão, após reclamações de bloqueios, suspensão de contas, remoções de publicações e restrições de alcance. Segundo o documento do MPF, com data de terça-feira, os procuradores receberam uma representação formulada por organizações que monitoram o trabalho das "big techs" relatando "volume expressivo de notícias (mais de 1.000 casos registrados) de bloqueios, suspensão de contas, remoções de publicações e restrições de alcance promovidos por plataformas digitais -- especialmente a Meta (Instagram, Facebook e WhatsApp) e o X -- contra cidadãos, jornalistas, comunicadores, veículos independentes de imprensa, entidades estudantis e movimentos sociais". Uma das organizações que assinam o pedido, a CTRL+Z, detalha em seu site que, além de já ter documentado mais de 1.000 casos de restrições e banimentos, 22% dos casos documentados são de contas ou postagens censuradas sem explicação –- o que tem afetado, além de cidadãos comuns, também movimentos sociais e estudantis, segundo a entidade. Procuradas, a Meta e o X não responderam de imediato a pedido de comentário. A subprocuradora-geral da República Paula Bajer Fernandes, procuradora federal adjunta dos Direitos do Cidadão, determinou o envio de ofício à Meta para que informe em cinco dias como é feito o monitoramento, detalhando os episódios reportados. Por ora, não houve providências a serem adotadas pelo X, conforme o documento. A representante do MPF pede para que se informe, entre outras questões, a natureza, data, duração e motivação específica de cada medida de restrição aplicada aos perfis listados na representação; se o bloqueio decorreu de ordem judicial específica ou de moderação automatizada própria baseada em algoritmos; se houve notificação prévia/concomitante, a motivação individualizada e o canal de recurso efetivo ao usuário afetado; e, por último, a existência de mecanismos internos de auditoria e correção de erros de moderação em massa. A campanha do presidente e candidato à reeleição Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) tem criticado a atuação da Meta e chegou a acionar o Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) pelo que considera "seletividade algorítmica", apontando disparidade no tratamento dado às campanhas dele e a do senador de oposição Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), seu adversário no segundo turno.

item.title: US Transportation Secretary meeting with Boeing, GE CEOs on aircraft certification reform efforts
item.description: US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy on Wednesday is meeting with the CEOs of major aerospace companies including Boeing and GE on his efforts to reform new aircraft certification, officials said.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy on Wednesday is meeting with the CEOs of major aerospace companies including Boeing (BA.N) and GE (GE.N) on his efforts to reform new aircraft certification, officials said. On Sept. 30, Duffy said he wants to speed certification of new airplanes from Boeing and other manufacturers, citing competition concerns from China. Approving a new airplane can take five or more years and require substantial testing and data and extensive documentation. The Federal Aviation Administration in June proposed changes to modernize and speed certification of new commercial airplanes. A spokesperson for Duffy confirmed he was meeting with industry executives. Boeing and GE declined to comment. "If we can't move at a different pace in certification, we're going to lose. China is going to beat us. We're going to lose not because you don't have the innovation," Duffy told reporters last month, warning that private capital is not going to invest in innovation because it is going to take a decade for approvals. The effort could be a boost to manufacturers like Boeing (BA.N) Airbus (AIR.PA) Embraer (EMBJ3.SA) and Bombardier (BBDb.TO) . It took Boeing over eight years to get the smaller 737 MAX 7 certified, which was finally approved in August. The certification of the 777x is more than five years behind Boeing's original schedule. FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford has pushed for reforms to certification and disclosed earlier this year the agency has a few projects working with industry "to see how they can streamline the process." The prior FAA head, Mike Whitaker, told Reuters in 2024 that the agency was looking at using better technology to streamline the process. Reuters first reported the FAA's planned changes in September, disclosing the agency planned to reduce the number of "exemptions, special conditions, and equivalent level of safety findings required during the certification process." Duffy also urged more entrants in commercial space. "It needs to be more vibrant. We need more competition, more players," Duffy said, adding the government is also trying to move faster in space to speed innovation.

item.title: US judiciary to weigh broadcasting federal trials for crime victims
item.description: A US judicial rulemaking panel is considering whether to create a narrow exception to the longstanding ban on TV and audio broadcasts of federal criminal trials to allow victims to watch the proceedings remotely.
item.dc:creator: Nate Raymond
item.content:encoded: A US judicial rulemaking panel is considering whether to create a narrow exception to the longstanding ban on TV and audio broadcasts of federal criminal trials to allow victims to watch the proceedings remotely. The proposal was discussed during a meeting in Boston of the US Judicial Conference's Advisory Committee on Criminal Rules, which only two years ago [USN:L1N3MD1SL TEXT:"voted against"] a request by media organizations to more broadly lift the ban against broadcasting federal criminal proceedings. Most state courts already allow televised trials. Following the COVID-19 pandemic, federal courts have permitted remote audio access to proceedings in civil and bankruptcy cases when testimony is not being taken. But the federal judiciary had held firm on the broadcasting ban in criminal cases, which dates back to 1946. Judges in 2024 cited concerns about how to protect the privacy of witnesses and jurors in deciding to maintain the bar on cameras. Recently, though, Senior US District Judge Michael Mosman of Oregon, the committee's chair, appointed Debevoise & Plimpton partner [USN:KBN1392KR TEXT:"Mary Jo White"], the former chair of the US Securities and Exchange Commission, to head a subcommittee that would consider a narrow lifting of the ban. Chicago-based US District Judge Edmond Chang last year suggested amending the rule to permit victims and third-party custodians at bail hearings to watch criminal case proceedings remotely. Chang did so after finding that he was barred in one narcotics-related case from allowing the mother of a victim who died of an overdose to listen to a sentencing hearing via a closed-circuit feed from Arizona, where she lived, even though both the prosecution and defense supported giving her that option. Congress has twice allowed such closed-circuit televising of criminal proceedings for victims' benefit, starting with the 9/11 Victims Access Act of 2002, which allowed them to watch the case against Zacarias Moussaoui, the only person ever convicted in a US court in connection with al Qaeda's September 11, 2001 attacks. Congress later passed the Lockerbie Victims Access Act, which was enacted in 2024 and allows victims and family members to watch from afar the [USN:S0N43J05A TEXT:"criminal trial proceedings"] scheduled for next year in Washington, DC, of a former Libyan intelligence operative accused of building the bomb that brought down Pan Am Flight 103 over Lockerbie, Scotland, in 1988. White said her panel plans to meet in November and would also look at whether family members of defendants should be given the ability to watch proceedings remotely as well. The panel would also examine what restrictions would be imposed, such as if an out-of-state victim would need to watch any broadcast from within their local federal courthouse. But White noted the limits of any exception her panel may ultimately recommend, noting that the two earlier laws gave judges the discretion to still bar broadcasting entirely "in order to protect the defendant's right to a fair trial." Read more: [USN:L1N3MD1SL TEXT:"Panel votes to maintain ban on cameras in US federal criminal trials"] [USN:L1N3AO2H5 TEXT:"US federal courts to allow limited remote audio access post-pandemic"] (This story has been refiled to specify federal trials in the headline.)

item.title: Quênia confirma segundo caso de Ebola, um parente do primeiro paciente
item.description: O Quênia registrou um segundo caso de Ebola na quarta-feira, cerca de uma semana após registrar seu primeiro caso de infecção pela doença viral, quando um queniano que morava no Congo morreu em um hospital de Nairóbi no dia 5 de outubro.
item.dc:creator: Humphrey Malalo, Vincent Nzilani
item.content:encoded: O Quênia registrou um segundo caso de Ebola na quarta-feira, cerca de uma semana após registrar seu primeiro caso de infecção pela doença viral, quando um queniano que morava no Congo morreu em um hospital de Nairóbi no dia 5 de outubro. O segundo paciente, um homem de 39 anos, é parente próximo do primeiro caso e já estava em quarentena quando adoeceu na terça-feira, informou o Ministério da Saúde em comunicado. Segundo o comunicado, ele foi isolado imediatamente após apresentar sintomas, incluindo febre, fadiga e dores nas articulações. “Ambos os casos estão relacionados, e não há evidências de disseminação na comunidade em geral”, afirmou o ministério. O segundo caso, no entanto, aumentará as preocupações no Quênia, o quarto país a registrar um caso relacionado à epidemia de Ebola no Congo — a segunda maior já registrada globalmente, com mais de 9.000 casos e mais de 4.000 mortes. O primeiro caso surgiu depois que um queniano, que havia adoecido no Congo cerca de um mês antes de viajar por estrada para Uganda, voou para Nairóbi em 3 de outubro, onde um parente o levou de carro ao hospital. Esse caso gerou preocupações quanto a falhas nos sistemas de triagem nas fronteiras da região, já que o paciente conseguiu cruzar a fronteira entre o Congo e Uganda, que está fechada desde maio. As autoridades quenianas localizaram 113 dos 128 contatos do primeiro paciente, com 108 pessoas em quarentena. “Os outros cinco estão fora do Quênia, e as autoridades de saúde desses países foram informadas... O rastreamento dos 15 restantes continua”, informou o ministério. As autoridades também estão realizando avaliações de todas as pessoas que tiveram contato com o segundo paciente desde o surgimento de seus sintomas, incluindo profissionais de saúde e funcionários do centro de quarentena. “Essa é a resposta funcionando conforme planejado”, acrescentou o ministério, informando que compartilhará atualizações sobre a evolução do paciente. Ele pediu aos quenianos que mantenham a calma, mas permaneçam vigilantes. O Ebola se espalha por contato direto com fluidos corporais de pessoas infectadas, vivas ou mortas. A doença pode causar febre, vômito, diarreia e, em casos graves, hemorragias internas e externas.

item.title: Airbus terá em breve decisão sobre aumento de produção de jato A350
item.description: A Airbus planeja decidir “o mais rápido possível” sobre o aumento da capacidade de produção de seu jato de fuselagem larga A350, afirmou o presidente-executivo da divisão de aviação comercial do grupo, Lars Wagner.
item.dc:creator: Tim Hepher
item.content:encoded: A Airbus (AIR.PA) planeja decidir “o mais rápido possível” sobre o aumento da capacidade de produção de seu jato de fuselagem larga A350, afirmou o presidente-executivo da divisão de aviação comercial do grupo, Lars Wagner. A maior fabricante de aeronaves do mundo também está estudando ativamente versões maiores do A350 e do modelo menor, o A220, que vem gerando prejuízos, com decisões sobre ambos os projetos previstas para o início de um período de planejamento de cinco anos, disse ele. “A decisão de aumentar a taxa de produção do A350 é inevitável. Vamos fazê-lo porque o mercado claramente exige mais aeronaves”, disse Wagner a jornalistas. “É uma grande decisão, por isso precisamos levá-la ao conselho de administração. Mas isso vai acontecer mais cedo ou mais tarde.” A Airbus possui uma linha de montagem para o concorrente das séries 787 e 777 da Boeing, projetada para produzir de 12 a 13 jatos por mês. Aumentar essa produção exigirá uma nova linha e um novo sistema industrial, disse Wagner. Separadamente, o executivo disse que há “claramente demanda” por um A350 mais longo e com mais assentos, amplamente conhecido como A350-2000, e por uma versão maior do A220, de aproximadamente 130 assentos, conhecido como A220-500. O ex-presidente-executivo da MTU Aero Engines, que assumiu o comando da maior divisão da Airbus este ano, se recusou a dizer se a Airbus poderá abrir mão da posição de ter a Rolls-Royce (RR.L) como única fabricante de motores do A350 quando se trata de equipar a nova versão. Fontes do setor afirmam que a Airbus cogitou a possibilidade de usar um motor da GE Aerospace para o A350-2000, com cerca de 400 assentos, mas que o interesse da fabricante de motores tem sido discreto até o momento. Wagner reiterou que a Airbus está confiante em atingir as metas de entrega até o final do ano, apesar das recentes falhas de qualidade. A longo prazo, a Airbus continua considerando a data “teórica” de 2030 para o lançamento de um jato de corredor único totalmente novo, disse Wagner. O momento do lançamento dos sucessores das séries mais vendidas, o Boeing 737 e o Airbus A320, é uma das decisões mais aguardadas do setor, impulsionada em parte pelas pesquisas das empresas de motores. Alguns analistas estão céticos quanto à possibilidade da próxima geração de jatos tomar forma já em 2030, à medida que os fabricantes de motores aperfeiçoam tecnologias avançadas. O presidente-executivo da Boeing (BA.N) , Kelly Ortberg, disse à Aviation Week em julho que a próxima geração está “avançando na direção certa”. MOTORES PRATT & WHITNEY No curto prazo, a Airbus afirmou que continua enfrentando incertezas quanto ao fornecimento de motores Pratt & Whitney para os jatos da família A320. A Airbus e a subsidiária da RTX (RTX.N) vêm debatendo quem terá acesso prioritário ao fornecimento de motores, as fábricas de aeronaves ou as oficinas de reparo das companhias aéreas. A Airbus afirmou que ainda não chegou a um acordo com a Pratt sobre o fornecimento após 2026. “Estamos lidando com isso com muita seriedade junto à Pratt & Whitney e tentando avançar o máximo possível”, disse Florent Massou dit Labaquere, chefe de operações da Airbus. O número de aeronaves em serviço imobilizadas devido a atrasos no fornecimento de motores de reserva é “ainda bastante significativo”, acrescentou ele. A Reuters informou em março que a Airbus havia dado o pontapé inicial em uma ação por indenização por atrasos na entrega de motores, em uma disputa que pode chegar a bilhões de dólares. As negociações entre as duas empresas para evitar uma batalha judicial ainda não resultaram em avanços significativos, segundo fontes do setor. A Airbus acusou a Pratt de voltar atrás quanto ao número de motores alocados às suas fábricas. A Pratt, que fornece cerca de 40% dos jatos A320, informou que houve progresso na estabilização dos suprimentos. “A Pratt & Whitney aumentou as entregas anuais de novos motores desde 2019, superando o setor e nossa participação geral no mercado para a frota”, afirmou a RTX em comunicado enviado por email, acrescentando que continua a expandir a capacidade de manutenção. Massou disse, no entanto, que as interrupções no fornecimento de um modelo diferente de motor da Pratt para o A220 praticamente desapareceram. Os motores da Rolls-Royce também estão em dia após preocupações anteriores, mas os atrasos no fornecimento de assentos continuam sendo uma questão urgente para os jatos de fuselagem larga, acrescentou ele.

item.title: Federal judge blocks planned US farm agency reorganization
item.description: A federal judge on Tuesday blocked the US Department of Agriculture from proceeding with its planned agency reorganization, in a blow to President Donald Trump's sweeping overhaul of the executive branch.
item.dc:creator: Leah Douglas
item.content:encoded: A federal judge on Tuesday blocked the US Department of Agriculture from proceeding with its planned agency reorganization, in a blow to President Donald Trump's sweeping overhaul of the executive branch. The ruling from the District Court for the Northern District of California is a victory for unions that had [USN:L1N44T0OQ TEXT:"sued"] to block the reorganization effort, in part because employees said it would [USN:L6N43T0ZQ TEXT:"weaken"] agency services. The order halts reorganization efforts at several USDA agencies, including the Agricultural Research Service, Forest Service, Food and Nutrition Administration, and others. Judge Vince Chhabria said the agency was "reprogramming" congressional funds for the reorganization, or using money for a different purpose than it was intended. "Congress did not contemplate USDA using its appropriated funds to shut down offices or relocate employees," Chhabria wrote. The agency's [USN:L6N41613W TEXT:"reorganization "]effort has sought to move about 2,600 employees from the Washington region, as well as to consolidate agency offices across the country. Agency staff had [USN:L6N43T0ZQ TEXT:"warned"] that wide-scale employee departures because of the reorganization risked trade, foreign aid, nutrition and other programs. A USDA spokesperson said, “The Department is reviewing the Judge’s decision and will file its response with the Court." "The administration’s attempt to gut this essential agency is blatantly illegal, and we’re thankful the court has stopped it, for now, from proceeding with a reckless plan," said Patrick Moran, president of the American Federation of State, County & Municipal Employees, in a statement.

item.title: Los incendios en la Amazonía brasileña aumentan avivados por El Niño y el cambio climático
item.description: El Niño, el cambio climático y la actividad humana están provocando este mes un aumento de los incendios en el corazón de la Amazonía brasileña, mientras los bomberos se apresuran a contener las llamas, cuyo humo está asfixiando a los residentes y provocando la cancelación de eventos en las localidades cercanas.
item.dc:creator: Bruno Kelly
item.content:encoded: El Niño, el cambio climático y la actividad humana están provocando este mes un aumento de los incendios en el corazón de la Amazonía brasileña, mientras los bomberos se apresuran a contener las llamas, cuyo humo está asfixiando a los residentes y provocando la cancelación de eventos en las localidades cercanas. En las dos primeras semanas de octubre hubo 1.679 incendios en el estado brasileño de Amazonas, lo que supone un aumento del 253% en comparación con el mismo periodo del año pasado, según datos del sistema de vigilancia de la Amazonía del país. Los incendios, que las autoridades sospechan que fueron provocados, han llenado el cielo de columnas de humo y han provocado la declaración del estado de emergencia en al menos 36 municipios de Amazonas, causando problemas respiratorios a los residentes. "Nuestra situación aquí es crítica", dijo Luiz Rios, un agricultor jubilado del municipio de Autazes, en el estado de Amazonas, que ha tenido dificultades para respirar por las noches, lo que le ha provocado hinchazón en la cara. La mala calidad del aire provocada por los incendios ha obligado a cancelar eventos al aire libre en Manaos, la capital del estado con más de dos millones de habitantes, donde las escuelas públicas cerraron el miércoles. Agosto y septiembre suelen ser el punto álgido de la estación seca en la Amazonía, cuando los incendios se vuelven más difíciles de controlar, antes del inicio de la temporada de lluvias, que suele traer alivio en octubre. Este año, sin embargo, las lluvias han tardado. Científicos y autoridades señalan el fenómeno de El Niño, que se prevé que sea el más intenso jamás registrado, y el cambio climático como factores determinantes del aumento de los incendios. "El estrés hídrico y el estrés térmico están azotando con extrema intensidad, creando una situación potencialmente peligrosa que, agravada por la actividad humana, amenaza esta biodiversidad, la salud de las personas y la productividad de estas tierras", dijo Carlos Durigan, geógrafo e investigador del Instituto de Investigación Ambiental de la Amazonía.

item.title: Ações europeias têm leve alta após resultados sólidos da ASML e ganhos no setor de saúde
item.description: As ações europeias registraram ganhos modestos nesta quarta-feira, depois que resultados financeiros sólidos da ASML tranquilizaram investidores preocupados com a demanda por IA, enquanto as ações do setor de saúde atingiram seu maior nível em mais de cinco semanas.
item.dc:creator: Avinash P, Niket Nishant
item.content:encoded: As ações europeias registraram ganhos modestos nesta quarta-feira, depois que resultados financeiros sólidos da ASML tranquilizaram investidores preocupados com a demanda por IA, enquanto as ações do setor de saúde atingiram seu maior nível em mais de cinco semanas. O índice pan-europeu STOXX 600 (.STOXX) subiu 0,43%, para 637,75 pontos. O índice do setor de saúde (.SXDP) foi o que mais se valorizou no índice de referência, subindo 2,3% e atingindo seu maior nível desde 7 de setembro. Além disso, as ações da ASML (ASML.AS) subiram 1,2% após a empresa informar que os clientes já estavam buscando fazer pedidos de suas ferramentas avançadas de fabricação de chips para 2029 e 2030, o que demonstra que a demanda continua sólida. “A ASML ajudou a sustentar o argumento otimista de que as ações do setor de tecnologia continuam apresentando bom desempenho, a demanda por chips permanece forte e os gastos com infraestrutura provavelmente continuarão até bem depois de 2027”, disse Gordon Kerr, estrategista macroeuropeu da KBRA. Abalados por semanas de preços elevados do petróleo e rendimentos dos títulos públicos, os investidores europeus depositam suas esperanças nos lucros corporativos para dar um novo fôlego ao mercado de ações. Mas os resultados têm sido irregulares até o momento. No início desta semana, a LVMH (LVMH.PA) , referência no setor de luxo, divulgou vendas no terceiro trimestre abaixo do esperado, à medida que uma acentuada deterioração no ânimo dos consumidores chineses afetou a demanda por suas marcas principais. “Esperamos uma verdadeira dicotomia nos lucros”, disse Michael Field, estrategista-chefe de mercado de ações para a região EMEA da Morningstar, acrescentando que as empresas expostas a preços mais altos de energia e ao fraco ânimo do consumidor podem enfrentar dificuldades. As ações do setor de mineração (.SXPP) lideraram as perdas setoriais nesta quarta-feira, com a Fresnillo sendo a que mais ficou para trás, após uma queda de 4,6% quando o JPMorgan reduziu seu preço-alvo para a ação. O índice pan-europeu STOXX 600 (.STOXX) fechou em alta de 0,43%, a 637,75 pontos. Em LONDRES, o índice Financial Times (.FTSE) avançou 0,70%, a 10.724,86 pontos. Em FRANKFURT, o índice DAX (.GDAXI) subiu 0,15%, a 25.298,61 pontos. Em PARIS, o índice CAC-40 (.FCHI) ganhou 0,58%, a 7.873,11 pontos. Em MILÃO, o índice Ftse/Mib (.FTMIB) teve desvalorização de 0,61%, a 49.753,84 pontos. Em MADRI, o índice Ibex-35 (.IBEX) registrou alta de 0,10%, a 19.230,70 pontos. Em LISBOA, o índice PSI20 (.PSI20) valorizou-se 0,38%, a 9.415,66 pontos.

item.title: Zelenskiy diz que é "doloroso" quando Trump escolhe outro lado
item.description: O presidente da Ucrânia, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, disse em entrevista nesta quarta-feira que foi "doloroso" ver Donald Trump tomar outro lado na guerra em curso entre Ucrânia e Rússia, depois que o presidente dos EUA afirmou que Zelenskiy deveria ser substituído.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente da Ucrânia, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, disse em entrevista nesta quarta-feira que foi "doloroso" ver Donald Trump tomar outro lado na guerra em curso entre Ucrânia e Rússia, depois que o presidente dos EUA afirmou que Zelenskiy deveria ser substituído. Zelenskiy disse ao programa “Piers Morgan Uncensored”: “É doloroso quando o presidente Trump escolhe um lado, que não é o nosso.” Ele também disse que não se importava que Trump ficasse no meio entre a Ucrânia e a Rússia, mas acrescentou: “Se você está no meio, precisa permanecer no meio.” Questionado se se sentia traído por Trump, que no fim de semana pediu que a Ucrânia elegesse um novo presidente após ter concordado em suspender as sanções às exportações russas de diesel, Zelenskiy respondeu: “Na verdade, sim... mas é um pouco mais complicado do que apenas minhas emoções ou meus sentimentos.” “É uma pena estarmos perdendo um parceiro forte”, acrescentou. Zelenskiy também disse: “Não estamos vendendo nosso país... para nós, não se trata de negócios, é simplesmente a nossa vida e este é o nosso país.”

item.title: Governo anuncia medidas de apoio a produtoras de videogames no Brasil
item.description: O governo federal anunciou nesta quarta-feira regulamentação de um conjunto de medidas de apoio para a produção de videogames no Brasil, que inclui R$200 milhões para serem destinados a financiamento do desenvolvimento de jogos e soluções digitais inovadoras por meio da Financiadora de Estudos e Projetos (Finep).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O governo federal anunciou nesta quarta-feira regulamentação de um conjunto de medidas de apoio para a produção de videogames no Brasil, que inclui R$200 milhões para serem destinados a financiamento do desenvolvimento de jogos e soluções digitais inovadoras por meio da Financiadora de Estudos e Projetos (Finep). O conjunto de medidas vem em um momento em que o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva disputa o segundo turno da eleição presidencial deste ano com o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), cujo pai, Jair, reduziu Imposto de Importação de videogames quando estava à frente do Palácio do Planalto. As medidas anunciadas por Lula nesta quarta-feira também incluem facilitação do acesso de empresas brasileiras de games a crédito. "Será proposta pela Agência Nacional do Cinema (Ancine) ao Comitê Gestor do Fundo Setorial do Audiovisual (FSA) a redução do valor mínimo dos empréstimos de R$500 mil para a faixa de R$150 mil", afirmou o governo em comunicado à imprensa. A proposta também prevê reduzir os juros de TR mais 2% para TR mais 0,5% ao ano. Para 2026, o FSA prevê R$460 milhões em crédito para a indústria audiovisual, incluindo videogames. O governo também anunciou a modalidade "Rouanet Games" voltado à captação de patrocínios pela Lei Rouanet, em parceria com empresas públicas. O decreto reconhece que o setor de games pode acessar mecanismos federais de fomento de tecnologia, pesquisa, desenvolvimento, inovação e cultura e que caberá à Ancine regulamentar o acesso à Lei do Audiovisual e propor critérios de financiamento pelo FSA.

item.title: NWSL, USL to meet in new women's cup tournament
item.description: The NWSL and the USL Super League will compete in a new women's cup competition, U.S. Soccer announced on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The NWSL and the USL Super League will compete in a new women's cup competition, U.S. Soccer announced on Wednesday. The Arthur M. Blank Crest Cup will feature a $1.7 million prize pool, with the winner earning a berth to the Concacaf W Champions Cup. "Women's soccer continues to be one of the most dynamic and inspiring forces in sport," U.S. Soccer president Cindy Parlow Cone said in a statement. "The Crest Cup will create meaningful impact by bringing people together, attracting investment in the future of the game, and ensuring that excellence, inclusivity, and opportunity remain at the heart of women's soccer in the United States." U.S. Soccer did not confirm a start date for the tournament. ESPN previously reported that it is expected to launch in 2028. The single-elimination tournament will feature every team from NWSL (18 teams in 2028) and the USL Super League, which launched in 2024-25 and currently fields eight teams. Blank, who contributed $50 million to build the new U.S. Soccer National Training Center near Atlanta, is the owner of the NFL's Atlanta Falcons, Atlanta United FC of MLS, Atlanta City FC of NWSL and the TGL squad Atlanta Drive GC. --Field Level Media

item.title: Falcons QB Michael Penix Jr. (rib) likely to start Sunday
item.description: Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. will likely start Sunday if there are no setbacks with his rib injury, head coach Kevin Stefanski said Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. will likely start Sunday if there are no setbacks with his rib injury, head coach Kevin Stefanski said Wednesday. Penix is expected to practice on Wednesday as the Falcons (2-3) prepare for a home matchup against the Chicago Bears (3-2). The Bears are not ruling out Caleb Williams playing for the first time since injuring his hamstring Week 2. Williams was limited in practice last Friday, two days before Chicago's loss at Green Bay, and did footwork and agility drills on the field before the game. He's expected to increase activity following a walkthrough practice Wednesday and could play to push backup Tyson Bagent back to the bench. Penix sustained the injury late in the fourth quarter of last Sunday's 30-23 overtime loss to the Baltimore Ravens after taking a hit to the ribs on a sack by Tavius Robinson. Tua Tagovailoa replaced Penix in overtime and threw a game-ending interception on his second play. Penix, 26, missed the first two weeks of this season to complete his recovery from ACL surgery. He has completed 67.5% of his passes for 719 yards, three touchdowns and one interception while posting a 2-1 record in three starts. --Field Level Media

item.title: US lawmakers ask FAA to conduct review before allowing Amazon drone hub near Boston
item.description: A group of Democratic lawmakers on Wednesday urged the Federal Aviation Administration to conduct a new environmental review before allowing an Amazon Prime Air drone delivery hub to be located about 30 miles (48.28 km) west of Boston.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: A group of Democratic lawmakers on Wednesday urged the Federal Aviation Administration to conduct a new environmental review before allowing an Amazon Prime Air drone delivery hub to be located about 30 miles (48.28 km) west of Boston. Massachusetts Democratic US Senators Ed Markey and Elizabeth Warren and Representatives Jim McGovern and Lori Trahan wrote to FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford seeking a new review after communities raised concerns about the planned Westborough hub and its impact on the environment and residents’ quality of life, including noise pollution, health and safety, and privacy. The FAA said it would respond directly to the lawmakers. Amazon did not immediately comment. Here are more details: On September 28, a group of 15 states and a Texas county on Monday sued the FAA over the agency's environmental review of planned commercial drone package delivery rules. The agency in July issued a broad environmental review that allows qualifying drone operators to launch fleets without a site-specific environmental analysis. The states — including New York, California, Massachusetts, Wisconsin and Michigan — and Harris County, Texas, said the FAA violated the law by failing to adequately analyze the potential environmental impacts of expanded drone package delivery operations. Drone delivery operations are already happening in states including California, Texas, Arkansas, Florida and Utah under the waiver process. The FAA said last year that eliminating the need for waivers "will significantly expand the use-case for drone technologies in areas like: manufacturing, farming, energy production, filmmaking, and the movement of products including lifesaving medications." The FAA environmental review included reviewing the noise impacts of 1,150 average drone deliveries from a single hub. Drones would depart a hub and travel en route at an altitude of less than 400 feet (121 meters).

item.title: México exige que plataformas digitais protejam menores de conteúdo violento e sexual
item.description: A presidente do México, Claudia Sheinbaum, afirmou que assinará, nesta quarta-feira, um decreto presidencial exigindo que as plataformas digitais, incluindo redes sociais e sites de streaming, protejam crianças e adolescentes de conteúdos violentos, sexuais e outros conteúdos prejudiciais.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A presidente do México, Claudia Sheinbaum, afirmou que assinará, nesta quarta-feira, um decreto presidencial exigindo que as plataformas digitais, incluindo redes sociais e sites de streaming, protejam crianças e adolescentes de conteúdos violentos, sexuais e outros conteúdos prejudiciais. O decreto, que intensificará a fiscalização das grandes empresas de tecnologia na segunda maior economia da América Latina, surge após um ataque perpetrado por dois ex-alunos de 18 anos a uma escola de ensino médio no Estado de Coahuila, no norte do país, no início de outubro, que deixou uma pessoa morta e outras três feridas. As plataformas digitais terão um mês para se adequarem ao decreto, afirmou a assessora do governo Luisa Maria Alcalde. Sheinbaum acrescentou que, caso as empresas não cumpram o decreto, o governo apoiará um projeto de lei para punir as plataformas. Autoridades afirmaram que já se reuniram com representantes de Meta (META.O) , Microsoft (MSFT.O) , Apple (AAPL.O) , TikTok, Google (GOOGL.O) , X e Huawei para discutir o assunto. Essas empresas não responderam imediatamente aos pedidos de comentário. A iniciativa do México segue uma tendência global mais ampla de proteção de menores na internet, com governos na Europa e na Austrália reforçando a fiscalização das plataformas digitais e Estados dos EUA adotando uma série de medidas de segurança infantil. O Brasil também tomou medidas para fortalecer a proteção das crianças na internet. Tais medidas levantaram questões sobre como proteger menores ao mesmo tempo em que se salvaguarda a privacidade e a liberdade de expressão.

item.title: As Wall Street banks finance and adopt AI, risks mount on both fronts
item.description: Wall Street's biggest banks want to ride the AI wave without getting caught in its undertow, as the promise of a lucrative infrastructure boom collides with questions over returns and new security threats.
item.dc:creator: Manya Saini, Saeed Azhar, Tatiana Bautzer
item.content:encoded: Wall Street's biggest banks want to ride the AI wave without getting caught in its undertow, as the promise of a lucrative infrastructure boom collides with questions over returns and new [USN:L4N4511UB TEXT:"security threats"]. Executives at the largest US banks this week discussed the risks of AI agents acting on customers' behalf and the uncertainty surrounding demand for the capital and computing power needed to fuel the technology's rapid growth. "While we are proud of the privileged position we play in the AI investment cycle, no one knows how the demands for capital and compute will evolve as the broader AI ecosystem matures," Goldman (GS.N) CEO David Solomon said on a call with analysts. "That will only become clearer as technology and markets continue to develop. This uncertainty reinforces the importance of remaining vigilant around the types of activity we finance and how we manage risk." Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser does not believe that higher rates will slow down the investment in the AI infrastructure. "We're not seeing a slowdown in investment in the broader AI ecosystem. There's simply not enough compute," she said, referring to the processing power needed to develop and run AI models, supported by chips and data centers. CAPITAL BEHIND THE GREAT AI BUILDOUT The scale of investment in AI infrastructure is [USN:S0N43A006 TEXT:"unprecedented"]. Big Tech has [USN:L4N41D03U TEXT:"committed billions"] to building data centers, the backbone of the computing capacity needed to train and run generative AI models. For Wall Street, the buildout offers a chance to finance one of the biggest investment cycles in decades. Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan said the enormous amount of AI capital investment is important for the lender's investment-grade debt and leveraged finance businesses. Yet the financing opportunity hinges on several unknowns, from whether demand for computing power will keep pace with the industry's ambitious expansion plans to the returns data center projects can generate and the potential for local opposition. "The AI investment cycle has become a complicated macroeconomic force in its own right," Wells Fargo CEO Charlie Scharf told analysts on a post-earnings call. He added that the buildout presents both opportunities and risks, given the significant leverage used to finance it and upward pressure on prices in some industries and supply chains. "Having said this, the strength of the economy and the positive forces from these investments have thus far outweighed the potential downside," Scharf said. Elevated interest rates that stay higher for longer, or rise further, could increase financing costs for data center projects, squeeze returns and make it more expensive for borrowers to service debt. Morgan Stanley Chief Financial Officer Sharon Yeshaya said in an interview with Reuters that the bank was "very discerning" about the types of risks it was taking. "What you worry about is that peers and other firms allow for a loosening of credit standards, and that's kind of what creates the issue. We're very focused on making sure that we're not involved in those types of transactions." The bank's CEO Ted Pick told analysts the involvement in AI financing is "existential" for Morgan Stanley. Investors, too, are weighing the economic benefits of the AI boom against the risk of losses on loans to projects that fail to deliver expected returns. "To the extent that the tech spend is helping drive growth in the overall economy, that is a positive and material to the banks. If the credit exposure is directly related to certain projects like speculative data-center builds, it could lead to issues down the road," said Macrae Sykes, portfolio manager at Gabelli Funds, which holds several bank stocks. Other investors say that banks are better positioned to manage those risks than some fear, having tightened their risk management practices after the financial crisis. Dave Ellison, portfolio manager at Hennessy Funds, said banks have not abandoned the lessons of the crisis and are being more careful than investors fear. They are facilitating AI-related financing, but often as arrangers that distribute risk. RINGFENCING EMERGING AI RISKS Beyond financing the buildout, banks are deploying AI in hopes of cutting costs and boosting productivity, but the financial payoff remains difficult to quantify. "As important and dramatic and exciting as this theme is, it takes a long time to really do things that are visible at an institution of our size," JPMorgan CFO Jeremy Barnum said, adding that it is not a surprise that benefits are not yet observable in the bank's quarterly earnings. Citi's Fraser said the bank is already seeing clear effects of the use of AI, such as developing products at lower cost and up to 40% faster. The use of coding tools has eased development and reduced tech vendor expenses by 30%, she said. "We are seeing the financial benefits from AI and automation significantly outweigh the investments we've made year to date," Fraser said. The bank is using AI to reduce the volume of manual processes, as well as response time in client service. Investors are betting on AI to deliver productivity gains across corporate America and valuations of US stocks leave little room for those gains to disappoint. "If those gains in productivity and lower costs do not arrive by the end of next year, investors will begin to question the hype of AI," Brian Mulberry, chief market strategist at Zacks Investment Management, said. At the same time, AI agents introduce new security challenges as they gain the ability to act autonomously. The technology is also adding to the threat posed by external cyber attackers. JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon said that the lender is developing tools to navigate agentic AI risk.

item.title: US individual health insurance enrollment fell to 20.5 million as of June, KFF says
item.description: Affordable Care Act and other individual health insurance plan enrollment fell 18% to 20.5 million members in June, according to health policy research firm KFF, marking the steepest annual decline since 2015 as Americans struggle with rising health insurance costs.
item.dc:creator: Amina Niasse
item.content:encoded: Affordable Care Act and other individual health insurance plan enrollment fell 18% to 20.5 million members in June, according to health policy research firm KFF, marking the steepest annual decline since 2015 as Americans struggle with rising health insurance costs. Enrollment was 25.2 million in the year-earlier period, KFF said. The 2010 Affordable Care Act, passed under Democratic President Barack Obama, created income-based government-subsidized health plans for individuals, commonly known as Obamacare. Millions have dropped coverage this year after extra [USN:L6N3XF1BG TEXT:"COVID-19 pandemic subsidies expired"], doubling or even tripling costs for some people. A previous KFF study found enrollment declined 12% year-over-year in February. KFF's analysis of the individual health insurance market also includes plans sold directly by insurers and those not regulated by the ACA, such as short-term coverage, a KFF spokesperson said. US Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. also said in a Wednesday press briefing that about 20 million people currently rely on Obamacare. KFF said plan members are expected to continue falling off the rolls through 2026. Some 17% of members enrolled in Obamacare plans say they are not confident they can pay premiums through the year, according to a KFF March survey. Insurers such as Centene (CNC.N) and UnitedHealth (UNH.N) have flagged rising medical costs in their Obamacare businesses this year. Companies offering the plans asked for a median rate hike of 14% this year, the [USN:L1N4390QG TEXT:"second-highest"] increase for premiums in nearly a decade. Insurers asking for higher payments pointed to a sicker or higher-risk mix of patients enrolled in the plans. KFF's study analyzed insurer marketplace enrollment reported in regulatory filings.

item.title: Wall Street banks see robust deal pipeline despite market volatility
item.description: Wall Street banks struck an optimistic tone on investment banking activity, citing robust deal pipelines and continued client engagement, even as rising bond yields and market volatility threaten to delay transactions.
item.dc:creator: Arasu Basil, Prakhar Srivastava
item.content:encoded: Wall Street banks struck an optimistic tone on investment banking activity, citing robust deal pipelines and continued client engagement, even as rising bond yields and market volatility threaten to delay transactions. Top banking executives said this week the environment for investment banking remains solid as businesses look to get deals done, with strategic dialogue inside corporate boardrooms remaining active. "Given the rate selloff, you're going to have the market take a little bit of a breath and a pause to make sure buyers and sellers can meet on valuation terms. We did see a little bit of that slowdown in the second half of September," JPMorgan Chief Financial Officer Jeremy Barnum said. "Big picture, I would lean more on the side of delayed rather than canceled. There are a lot of deals that need to get done that want to get done." Investment banking fees rose across most major US banks in the third-quarter, with Bank of America emerging as the outlier. "It's a solid pipeline. The US is the center of the action for both advisory and capital markets. We're seeing a bit of pickup in Europe and Asia, but a lot of this is about the US," Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser said. The overall sentiment for dealmaking is constructive, Fraser said, pointing to continued capital expenditure and elevated strategic discussions among clients. From tariffs to the conflict in the Middle East, Wall Street's investment banking machine has navigated several roadblocks over the past year and so, prompting brief bouts of caution but none have proved enough to derail the dealmaking recovery. "Strategic investors have resumed discussions for deals over the last weeks," said Morgan Stanley CFO Sharon Yeshaya. Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon also said companies were comfortable with the regulatory environment for dealmaking. "I don't sense that people are sitting on the sidelines because of the midterms," he said. Despite strong deal pipelines, Wall Street analysts remain cautious about near-term investment banking activity as higher borrowing costs and valuation uncertainty threaten to delay transactions. [USN:L6N45O096 TEXT:"Global M&A volumes"] fell 41% from the prior three months to $993 billion in the third quarter, falling below $1 trillion for the first time since the second quarter of 2025 as the number of megadeals shrank, LSEG data showed. IPO MARKET FACES FRESH HURDLES US IPO activity has lost momentum since the summer, as volatile markets and valuation concerns make investors more selective and complicate plans to go public. A string of postponements by high-profile hopefuls, including nuclear technology company [USN:L4N4581N6 TEXT:"Holtec"] and smart ring maker [USN:L4N45L0SK TEXT:"Oura"], has weighed on the fall IPO market. SoftBank-backed SB Energy has also [USN:L6N45E108 TEXT:"delayed launching its US IPO roadshow"]. "Things got a little bit softer in September. The IPO market was wide open. It's just if you expected a valuation and you got something 10% to 15% less," Goldman's Solomon said.
